Title: FGVPI targets RM1bil profit before tax by 2030
Article:
BANGI: FGV Palm Industries Sdn Bhd (FGVPI) is targeting RM1 billion in profit before tax by 2030, driven by a strategic shift in its business model and improved operational productivity.
FGVPI chief executive officer Hamdan Ismail said the company is currently transitioning from its traditional role as a primary processor to a "buy fruit, sell oil" business model, which is expected to begin on Oct 1.
He said the strategic roadmap includes progressively increasing its profit-before-tax target to RM400 million in 2027, RM600 million in 2028, RM800 million in 2029, and RM1 billion the following year.
"I have calculated this trajectory based on the shift in our business operations. By moving towards direct oil sales, we are positioning FGVPI as a high-value profit-generating entity," he said in his speech at a ceremony to present non-formal education recognition with the Malaysia Productivity Corporation here today.
FGVPI is a subsidiary of FGV Holdings Bhd that operates 63 palm oil mills nationwide, making it one of Malaysia's largest palm oil mill operators, responsible for processing fresh fruit bunches from smallholders and Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA) settler communities.
To drive this growth, Hamdan said RM45 million has been allocated for human capital development involving its 5,800 employees, with a focus on increasing annual productivity by 30 per cent.
"I want to see a 30 per cent increase in productivity. It may seem difficult, but I have done the calculations on paper and it is achievable.
"Competent workers will lead to efficient operations. Efficient operations will certainly increase productivity, which in turn will strengthen FGV's competitiveness," he said.
On operational excellence, Hamdan said FGVPI had maintained an oil extraction rate of more than 21 per cent at all its mills nationwide, with the Chuping Palm Oil Mill recording the highest rate at 24 per cent.
Hamdan said FGVPI, as one of the country's leading palm oil industry players, would also step up efforts to raise its palm kernel recovery rate beyond the five per cent target to increase returns to FELDA settlers.
"Although the industry average is low, FGV, as a leading player, must strive to exceed the five per cent target to enable higher fruit prices.
"Higher returns to settlers will help keep the economic cycle moving, while contributing to the well-being of millions of FELDA settlers and the wider FELDA community," he said.

Title: Court upholds RM900k payout to businessman over Bentley accident
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld a High Court decision ordering an insurance company to pay a businessman RM900,000 in indemnity for damage to his Bentley Continental GTS V6 MDS in an accident six years ago.
A three-member bench led by judge Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, sitting with Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim, unanimously dismissed MSIG Insurance (M) Bhd's appeal against the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision last year.
The bench also dismissed Inderpal Singh's appeal seeking RM253,000 for loss of use and RM990,000 for loss of enjoyment of the Bentley.
Both appeals were dismissed with costs of RM50,000 each.
Choo, who read out the decision, said the trial judge had evaluated the evidence, made findings of fact, considered witness testimony and addressed the discrepancies raised.
The trial judge, he said, had explained in his grounds of judgment why he was inclined to accept the plaintiff's (Inderpal) expert opinion and evidence, despite two opposing views.
"We found nothing plainly wrong which warrants this court to interfere with the findings.
"Although there was a version put forward by the defendant (MSIG) as to how the accident could have happened, that could not move this court to disturb the trial court's finding.
"It has to be something so clearly wrong, not just a mere probability the trial judge could be wrong," he said.
Choo said it was the defendant's theory that the plaintiff had staged the accident.
However, he said the court was not convinced by the suggestion that the accident had been staged to make an insurance claim.
"This is simply because there was no convincing evidence that the plaintiff had staged the accident, other than the defendant's submission that the accident could not have happened in the manner as proffered by the plaintiff.
"Occasionally, accidents could happen without a scientific and logical explanation," he said.
Choo said the bench also agreed with the High Court that the plaintiff had failed to prove that MSIG had been negligent in investigating the accident and processing his insurance claim.
Lawyers David Samuel and Mithurran Ravinthiran represented Inderpal, while Samreet Singh Sagoo and Theebadarshini Retnakumar acted for MSIG.
The matter arose after MSIG rejected Inderpal's claim for damage to the Bentley, which was comprehensively insured for RM900,000 from Feb 8, 2019 to Feb 7, 2020.
The Bentley was damaged in a single-vehicle accident at Jalan Tropicana Utama in Petaling Jaya on Jan 22, 2020.
At 11.31pm, Inderpal drove from his sister's residence in Kelana Jaya towards his home at Tropicana Golf & Country Resort.
While negotiating a right-hand bend along Jalan Tropicana Utama in light rain or drizzle, he encountered a puddle of water and a dog crossing his path.
The Bentley lost control, struck the guardrail on the left side of the road, passed beneath or through the weakened guardrail structure and came to rest behind it.
The next day, he notified MSIG's insurance agent and was advised to lodge a police report and send the Bentley to an authorised workshop, which inspected the vehicle and assessed the repair cost at RM1,053,491.07.
MSIG later rejected the claim on June 4, 2021, alleging that the accident was suspicious and involved fraudulent means, cheating, criminal breach of trust and the provision of false information.
However, the High Court, in its judgment dated May 20 last year, found that the accident occurred as reported and that MSIG had failed to prove that the claim was fraudulent.
Samreet had contended that the plaintiff failed to prove that the incident was an accidental collision.
After the proceedings, David said the evidence did not support the allegation that Inderpal had staged an elaborate scheme to defraud the insurance company.
He said the Court of Appeal was right not to overturn the High Court's findings, which he described as well-founded.
Inderpal was not present in court today.

Title: Tonibung renewable energy project wins national award
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A renewable energy project benefiting more than 20 households and shared community facilities in a remote Ranau village has earned Sabah-based Indigenous-led social enterprise Tonibung a national award.
Tonibung founder Adrian Banie Lasimbang said the project's success was driven not only by technology but also by strong community involvement in managing the system.
"For Tonibung , a successful renewable energy project is 20 per cent technology and 80 per cent community organising.
"The technology must work, but long-term sustainability comes from participation, local governance, technical training and care for the watershed that supports the system," he said.
On Tuesday, Tonibung 's Walou Micro Hydro-Solar Hybrid Project in Kampung Walou, Ranau, was named the winner of Category 3: Renewable Energy - On-Grid (Local) at the National Energy Awards (NEA) 2026 ceremony in Kuala Lumpur.
The NEA is a national programme under the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra), recognising outstanding energy management, energy efficiency and renewable energy projects in Malaysia.
Under the NEA framework, winners in the main award categories represent Malaysia at the Asean Energy Awards, a regional recognition programme led by the ASEAN Centre for Energy.
Adrian, who is also Tonibung's technical director, said the project was jointly developed with Matahio Energy and the community.
The project began in 2024 and combines an upgraded 3kW micro-hydro plant with 20kWp of rooftop solar photovoltaic panels, 40kWh of lithium iron phosphate battery storage, smart hybrid inverters and digital monitoring supported by satellite internet.
The hybrid system provides 24-hour electricity, with micro-hydro supplying power when river flow is sufficient, while solar energy and battery storage maintain the supply during dry periods and periods of higher demand.
Previously, the community depended on diesel generators for electricity.
The project is expected to avoid about 7,300 litres of diesel use and 19.6 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually, while reducing household energy costs and the risks associated with transporting and storing fuel in the remote area.
The project is also centred around the Matahio Community Hall, whose rooftop was adapted for the solar panels after the community identified the need for a shared space.
The hall now provides internet access and serves as a venue for meetings, a monthly tamu, women vendors and small community businesses.
Community members also contributed through gotong-royong, established a village energy committee, appointed and trained local operators, and introduced metered electricity and tariff collection to support maintenance.
Tonibung director Alice Jipius said the award belonged to the Kampung Walou community, which contributed its time, labour and local knowledge and now manages the system itself.
"Walou shows that rural communities are not merely beneficiaries of renewable energy - they can be owners, operators and leaders of their own energy future," she said.
The Walou project marks Tonibung's fourth recognition at the awards.
In 2021, Tonibung won the Renewable Energy - On-Grid (Local Grid) category for the 5kW Kampung Tiku Micro Hydro Project in Ulu Papar, while its Kobulu Micro Hydro Project in Kampung Buayan was named runner-up in the same category in 2023.
In 2025, the Puneng Trusan Micro Hydro Project won the national category and later achieved first runner-up.

Title: AI boom drives Malaysia's 6pct GDP growth: HSBC senior economist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stronger-than-expected growth in the second quarter of 2026 is being powered by the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom, according to HSBC senior Asean economist Yun Liu.
The country's economy accelerated six per cent year-on-year in Q2, beating the Statistics Department's 5.8 per cent advance estimate and 5.4 per cent expansion in Q1.
Liu said stronger growth reflects Malaysia's deep integration into global electronics supply chains, which has positioned the country to benefit significantly from surging AI-related technology demand.
"Despite the energy crisis, Malaysia's Q2 final GDP growth accelerated to 6.0 per cent year-on-year, reflecting the diversity of its economy."
Liu said Malaysia's performance mirrors that of regional peers such as Singapore and Vietnam, which also have extensive electronics supply chains.
She said the strength of Malaysia's electronics trade was a key reflection of the AI-driven upswing.
"Amid the AI tech upswing, whoever gets the electronics supply chain controls the trade and sees strong growth," she said.
The growth story, however, extends beyond the electronics sector.
While services and construction growth moderated, both sectors remained resilient, providing additional support to the economy.
Liu said for the first half of 2026, Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent year-on-year, making it the third-fastest growing economy in Asean behind Vietnam at more than 8.0 per cent and Singapore at 6.1 per cent.
Malaysia's strong growth has also been accompanied by one of the lowest inflation rates in Asean, helped by government subsidies that have kept the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 a litre.
"Outside of growth, Malaysia's inflation is also one of the lowest in Asean, thanks to the generous subsidies that have maintained the RON95 price at RM1.99 a litre, which keeps a lid on inflation," Liu said.
With growth remaining strong and inflation benign, Liu said Bank Negara Malaysia has room to wait and assess developments despite rising global macroeconomic uncertainty.
"With strong growth and benign inflation outlook, Bank Negara can afford to wait and see, despite increasing global macro uncertainty," she said.
HSBC maintains its view that Bank Negara is likely to keep its policy rate unchanged in both 2026 and 2027.

Title: Teresa Kok denies ignoring Taman Desa security scheme memorandum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seputeh member of Parliament Teresa Kok has denied claims that she ignored a protest memorandum over a disputed neighbourhood security scheme in Taman Desa Phase 1.
She said enforcement decisions regarding guarded neighbourhood schemes fall within the jurisdiction of Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and relevant public service agencies.
Responding to statements by Taman Desa Phase 1 Residents Association (TDP1RA) president Frank Yeh, Kok said she was neither involved in DBKL's decision-making process nor informed beforehand about an official letter issued by DBKL's urban planning department.
"I wish to clarify that I was never informed of, nor did I receive, the letter issued by DBKL to TDP1RA," Kok posted on her Facebook page today.
"In these circumstances, it is unfair to suggest that I was responsible for, or involved in, DBKL's decision concerning the neighbourhood security scheme implemented by TDP1RA."
She said enforcement actions regarding guarded neighbourhood schemes fall strictly within the jurisdiction of local authorities and public service agencies.
"I am not the decision-maker in this matter... While I fully appreciate the concerns of residents regarding safety, all residents' associations are required to comply with applicable regulations imposed by DBKL, police, and the Fire and Rescue Department."
Kok also urged the association not to attribute DBKL's actions to her or create misunderstandings regarding her role.
She was responding to Yeh, who had called for a press conference today to allege that the six-term MP had remained silent on a memorandum submitted nearly two weeks ago.
Yeh claimed that DBKL's urban planning department issued a letter dated June 5 threatening to shut down the Phase 1 Guarded Neighbourhood Scheme, a move he warned directly jeopardises the safety of nearly 1,000 residents, 90 per cent of whom are senior citizens.
He said the scheme enjoys 81 per cent majority support among residents and alleged "double standards" by local authorities and the parliamentary constituency office, claiming other guarded neighbourhood schemes in the area operating with guideline violations have been left unchecked.
Kok added that she remains committed to serving all constituents fairly without favouring any particular group or association, calling for constructive engagement between residents and the relevant authorities to resolve the dispute.

Title: In-game rewards up for grabs for streamers of MPL MY S18
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports fans stand a chance to win a share of 100,000 Diamonds by watching MPL Malaysia Season 18 (MPL MY S18) live on Tonton.
The 'Tonton & Menang: MPL MY S18' contest runs from Aug 14 to Nov 1, with 40,000 Diamonds available throughout the Regular Season and another 60,000 Diamonds during the Final Week and Playoffs.
Viewers will earn one point for every minute spent watching MPL MY S18 content and matches live on Tonton.
Points will be calculated at the end of each weekend, with the leaderboard reviewed and reset every Monday, giving viewers a fresh opportunity to compete each week.
Winners will be determined based on the highest watch time recorded during each weekly competition period.
Tonton will then contact the winners regarding the prize redemption process through the MLBB app.
To take part, viewers can scan the QR code on the promotional poster or visit the 'Tonton & Menang: MPL MY S18' microsite on Tonton.
After logging into their Tonton accounts, viewers can watch MPL MY S18 matches live on the platform, with their viewing time automatically converted into points.
MPL MY S18 matches will be streamed live on Tonton every Friday, Saturday and Sunday from Aug 14 to Nov 1.

Title: Road safety: Govt identifies 99 accident blackspots
Article:
KUCHING:: The Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Works Ministry to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur, or blackspots, on federal roads nationwide.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by the ministry under the MYJalan initiative, systematically manages, analyses and displays road accident data, including locations where accidents frequently occur.
"An average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure," he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here today.
He said the integration of accident data from the Integrated Police Reporting System (IPRS), under the supervision of the police, enabled RAMS to facilitate more accurate and timely planning and implementation of road safety interventions.
"Accurate and quality data is an important basis for planning safer, more efficient and sustainable road infrastructure," he said.

Title: Generasi Keadilan calls on PKR members to voice people's concerns
Article:
AYER KEROH: Generasi Keadilan has called on PKR members to remain honest in conveying the people's concerns to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying genuine loyalty should also include the courage to speak up when necessary.
Its chairman, Yusmadi Yusoff, said support for Anwar and the Madani government should be accompanied by a willingness to raise concerns respectfully and responsibly.
"Loyalty to a leader is measured not only by our courage to defend him when attacked, but also by our courage to tell him the truth before it is too late," he said in a statement today.
The statement was issued ahead of the 2026 Generasi Keadilan Conference, which will be held here tomorrow in conjunction with PKR's national congress on Aug 15 and 16.
Yusmadi, a former Balik Pulau member of parliament, said bringing a reformist leader to Putrajaya was a historic achievement, but the next challenge was to ensure the reform agenda translated into meaningful improvements in the lives of ordinary Malaysians.
"We have brought a reformer to Putrajaya. Now, we must bring reform to the people," he said.
He said this included ensuring that farmers, Felda settlers, workers, youths, students, people with disabilities, the people of Sabah and Sarawak, and ordinary families benefited from reforms undertaken by the government.
Yusmadi said Generasi Keadilan was neither a "nostalgia club" nor a platform to demand positions or form another faction within the party.
Instead, he said the group sought to serve as a bridge between the history and future of reform, the party leadership and grassroots, as well as the government and the people.
Yusmadi also outlined three priorities for the movement — bringing Reformasi closer to the people through service and problem-solving, uniting the experience of veterans with the energy of younger members and women, and ensuring power continued to be exercised as a public trust rather than a privilege.
"The true test of reform is not when we demand power, but when we are entrusted with power," he said.
He said the party should use its national congress to strengthen internal unity, return politics to serving the people and ensure the reform struggle continued to be carried forward by the next generation.

Title: Petronas Chemicals' earnings may peak in Q2 FY26
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) is expected to see its earnings peak in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 FY26).
This will be supported by stronger petrochemical prices despite lower plant utilisation from planned turnarounds, according to RHB Research.
The firm said PetChem's full-quarter benefit from elevated average selling prices (ASPs) should more than offset the temporary impact of lower utilisation.
It maintained its "Buy" call on PetChem with a target price (TP) of RM5.92, implying about 30 per cent upside.
RHB Research expects PetChem's Q2 core profit after tax and minority interest (Patmi) to surge to between RM700 million and RM1.1 billion, compared with RM242 million in Q1.
It said fertilisers and methanol (F&M) are likely to remain the key earnings driver, with stronger realised ASPs and wider product spreads more than offsetting utilisation estimated at about 80 per cent due to planned turnarounds at Asean Bintulu Fertiliser and Kertih.
It noted that Q2 is likely the earnings high watermark before normalisation from the second half of 2026 (2H26) onwards.
RHB Research said product prices strengthened materially quarter-on-quarter in the Q2 across both F&M and olefins and derivatives (O&D).
F&M benchmark prices averaged US$680 per tonne for urea, US$728 per tonne for ammonia and US$611 per tonne for methanol.
This represents increases of 27.9 per cent, 54.1 per cent and 56.9 per cent respectively from the previous quarter.
Meanwhile, prices of key O&D products also rose, with ethylene, monoethylene glycol, polyethylene and paraxylene increasing 27.2 per cent, 18.6 per cent, 25.9 per cent and 14.9 per cent respectively.
RHB Research noted that while the surge in F&M prices only emerged towards the end of Q1, PetChem captured the elevated pricing environment throughout the Q2 before prices moderated towards the end of June.
The weaker ringgit is also expected to provide an additional boost to reported earnings, with the average US dollar versus ringgit exchange rate rising to 4.00 in Q2 from 3.97 in Q1.
RHB said this would provide a translation benefit given PetChem's net US dollar exposure.
Looking ahead, RHB expects petrochemical prices to remain supported in 2H26, although they are likely to moderate from their second-quarter peaks.
It said urea prices have recovered to about US$445 per tonne from US$407.50 following a sharp correction from the April peak, supported by seasonal fertiliser demand.
"With the Hormuz Strait disruption still unresolved, we expect ongoing supply-side tightness to support prices and see urea recovering towards US$500 per tonne in 2H26," it said.
RHB Research also said the anticipated earnings recovery should support a gradual improvement in return on equity, justifying the use of the historical mean valuation multiple.
The valuation also incorporates a four per cent environmental, social and governance discount, reflecting PetChem's ESG score of 2.8 versus the country median of 3.0.
The firm has identified lower sales volume, a weaker-than-expected recovery in petrochemical spreads and a strengthening ringgit as key downside risks.

Title: Negri MB defends Seremban council's "cash for stray dogs" initiative
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan government wants the public to view the Seremban City Council's (MBS) 'cash for capture' initiative for stray dogs in a positive light, describing it as a proactive move to manage the state's stray population.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim welcomed MPS' initiative, saying that it is related to public safety.
"MBS undertook this programme as there was a need for it. If there are too many (stray dogs) to the extent that it poses a danger to the public and causes traffic mishaps, it should be acted upon.
"Our focus now is on the safety of all, not just any specific groups. Public safety is our priority.
"We want to see the people of Negri Sembila live in peace and harmony. If there are any threats to peace, we have to act accordingly in accordance with the law," he said.
He was speaking to the people after attending the state-level civil servants assembly and launch of the 'Kibar Jalur Gemilang 2026' campaign at the Dewan Majlis Bandaraya Seremban here today.
Also present were state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and other exco members.
Yesterday, Seremban Mayor Datuk Masri Baharuddin defended the programme, saying it was meant to improve the level of cleanliness, safety and welfare of the community via more systematic and effective stray animal management.
The programme offers cash incentives, namely RM50 per adult stray dog and RM25 for each puppy under six months old.
Ismail said the state government's priority was to ensure that the people of the state live in comfort and safety.
"The people must feel safe if they want to go to the mosque, the shops, for recreation and for their daily affairs. If there are threats such as uncontrolled wild dogs, then it's something we must address.
"This may not have been a big problem once, but now it is. We have to take appropriate action."
The initiative, named "Program Pemberian Insentif Penyerahan Anjing Terbiar Secara Sukarela 2026", was criticised by animal rights groups who said it encourages pet theft and exposes the public to unnecessary risks.
On Thursday, Lawyers for Animal Rights (LAR) said the Veterinary Services Department (DVS) classifies dog catching as hazardous work requiring trained personnel, yet MBS was offering incentives to members of the public to capture stray dogs.
The programme, it said, allows applicants to surrender unlicensed dogs based solely on self-declaration, without proper verification.
"A dog without a licence is not necessarily an ownerless dog. LAR is worried the bounty encourages pet theft without microchip or ownership checks," it said.
LAR also claimed that animal welfare non-governmental organisations specialising in rescue and Trap-Neuter-Release-Manage programmes had been excluded from the initiative.
It called on MBS to withdraw the scheme and disclose its legal authority, budgetary approvals, Animal Welfare Act licensing compliance, capture standard operating procedures and dog disposal plans.

Title: Penang church marks 240 years of Catholic heritage through two world wars
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Church of the Assumption will mark its 240th anniversary tomorrow, having survived two world wars and helped shape Catholic life and education in Penang.
Founded in 1786 by French missionary Reverend Father Arnold Garnault with the island's pioneer Eurasian community, the church is Penang's oldest Catholic church and a mother parish from which Catholicism spread across the northern region.
Its legacy helped shape the Roman Catholic Diocese of Penang, which today serves Penang, Perlis, Kedah, Perak and Kelantan.
The church was initially established on Church Street before the present building along Farquhar Street was constructed in 1860 under Reverend Father Claude Manissol.
It later became the cathedral and "Mother Church" of the Diocese of Penang from 1955 to 2003, before the bishop's seat was moved to the Cathedral of the Holy Spirit in Green Lane.
City Parish parish priest Reverend Father Edmund Woon said the 240th anniversary was a significant milestone for the Catholic community.
"We give thanks that through the grace and mercy of God, we are able to celebrate 240 years of history for this church.
"For more than two centuries, the church has withstood the test of time by surviving two world wars and many difficult periods, yet she has been able to continuously contribute towards the welfare of the people of Penang," he told the New Straits Times.
The church's history is closely intertwined with the development of Catholic education in Malaysia.
In 1825, then parish priest Bishop Jean Baptiste Boucho established a Catholic Free School and later invited the La Salle Brothers and Infant Jesus Sisters to Penang, contributing to the establishment of St Xavier's Institution and the former Convent Light Street in 1852.
The church's heritage also extends to music, with its historic pipe organ, procured from Morton and Moody in England in 1914 and installed in 1916.
The instrument, restored in England in 2013, is regarded as the second oldest playable pipe organ in Malaysia and remains in use during Sunday services.
Two wings were added to the church in 1928, expanding its seating capacity and giving the building its present cruciform layout.
The church survived the Second World War, although it was largely closed during the Japanese Occupation, with only a few services held.
It underwent a 14-month restoration beginning in September 2016 and reopened on Jan 1, 2018, with a rededication ceremony.
The adjacent Penang Diocesan Museum was also officially opened that year.
The church's connection with Penang's Eurasian community will be highlighted during tomorrow's anniversary celebration with the unveiling of a commemorative plaque at its garden, recognising the community's role in its establishment.
The Penang Eurasian Association will also hold a Eurasian Fiesta at the Assumption Church Hall from 11am to 6pm tomorrow, celebrating the community's culinary traditions, music and heritage.
The Church of the Assumption is also one of six major houses of worship along George Town's Street of Harmony, reflecting the city's history of religious diversity and coexistence.
The anniversary celebrations will continue with an Assumption Church Choir concert on Aug 22, featuring the church's more than century-old pipe organ and sacred music.
Tomorrow's feast day programme will begin with the Rosary at 5.30pm, followed by Holy Mass at 6pm, presided over by Cardinal Datuk Seri Sebastian Francis, Bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Penang.
The Mass is expected to conclude about 7.15pm, followed by a cake-cutting ceremony and the unveiling of the commemorative plaque.

Title: Schools may close if API readings exceed 200
Article:
TAIPING: Schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200 may be closed at the discretion of the principal or headmaster, based on monitoring and advice from the state Education Department (JPN) and district Education Office (PPD).
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the Education Ministry (MOE) had existing guidelines on managing the effects of haze, including circulars issued in 2016, 2019 and 2023.
He said JPN and PPD would monitor haze conditions and API readings from time to time, while school administrators were responsible for making decisions based on local conditions and the advice received.
"If the API reading exceeds 100, schools will suspend outdoor activities involving pupils, while outdoor gatherings and sports activities are also advised to be postponed," he told reporters after the signing of a memorandum of understanding between Toyo Tyre Malaysia and Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP), here, today.
He was commenting on several areas nationwide that recorded unhealthy API readings yesterday.
Wong said the ministry would continue to monitor the haze situation through JPN and PPD to ensure the health and safety of pupils.
"JPN, PPD and school administrators have sufficient experience to make decisions from time to time and conduct continuous monitoring to safeguard the health of our children," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang MMEA detains Indonesian vessel over alleged illegal fishing
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained an Indonesian fishing vessel yesterday for allegedly encroaching into Malaysian waters and fishing without permission.
The unregistered wooden vessel was detected by the Penang MMEA during a routine patrol by KM Semilang.
Penang Maritime director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the vessel was intercepted at 11.20am, about 38 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Kendi.
"Checks found that the unregistered wooden vessel originated from Pantai Labu, Medan, Indonesia, and was operated by five Indonesian crew members aged between 17 and 44," he said today.
The crew comprised a skipper and four deckhands.
Suffi said further checks found that all five failed to produce valid identification documents and did not have valid documents or permission to enter Malaysia.
He said they were also suspected of fishing in Malaysian waters without written permission from the director-general of the Fisheries Department.
"The crew were detained for alleged offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for failing to possess valid identification documents and the Fisheries Act 1985 for fishing in Malaysian waters without authorisation.
"The total value of the vessel, fishing equipment and catch seized was estimated at RM3 million," he added.
Suffi said the latest detention brought the number of foreign fishing vessels detained by Penang MMEA between Jan 1 and July 31 this year to five, following sustained enforcement operations in Malaysian waters.
The vessel, crew, fishing equipment and seized catch were escorted to the Limbongan Batu Maung Jetty before being handed over to the Penang Maritime investigation officer for further investigation.
MMEA said it would continue to strengthen patrols and surveillance to curb illegal fishing and protect Malaysia's sovereignty and marine resources.
The public can report maritime criminal activities or emergencies to the Penang Maritime Operations Centre at 04-262 6146 or the MERS 999 emergency line.

Title: PKR members leaving for Bersama have little impact on party - Youth chief
Article:
AYER KEROH: The departure of some PKR members to join Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has had minimal impact on the party and has not disrupted its organisation, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He confirmed that some members had applied to leave PKR after losing confidence in the party and choosing to join Bersama, which has been taken over by former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli.
"Yes, I do not deny that there have been applications by party members to leave the party.
"Some gave the reason that they had lost confidence in the party and chose to be with the party (Bersama)," he told reporters during a press conference at the 2026 PKR Youth national congress here today.
Kamil said he did not know the percentage involved but maintained that the number was small and had not affected PKR's operations.
"It has not affected the running of PKR at all, and today we can see that the party remains strong," he said.
On Wednesday, Rafizi claimed thatPakatan Harapan's defeat in the Negri Sembilan election had prompted some members of its component parties to join Bersama.
Rafizi said the party had about 29,200 members nearly three months after its formation, with f
ormer PKR members accounting for about 25 per cent
.
Kamil, however, pointed to the turnout at this year's PKR Youth congress as an indication that grassroots members remained committed despite the party's recent electoral setbacks.
He said the participation reflected members' determination to continue strengthening PKR despite the recent setbacks and resulting dip in morale.
He said the emergence of new political parties was part of Malaysia's increasingly fluid political landscape since 2018, and PKR had no right to prevent any party from contesting elections.
Kamil acknowledged that Bersama could have some impact in constituencies where the two parties competed for similar groups of voters.
He cited Bukit Batu and Perling in the recent Johor election, where Bersama candidates were also fielded and PKR suffered narrow defeats.
"We do not deny that there was some impact because perhaps the voter segment is the same, as we saw in the Johor election," he said.
Kamil added that PKR would learn from the outcome, stressing that "every vote counts" and that the party needed to maximise support in closely fought seats.

Title: 1,259 e-waste containers targeted for shipment by year-end
Article:
KLANG: The Port Klang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) is targeting the shipment of 1,259 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) out of Malaysia by the end of this year through a joint operation involving various agencies.
Its commander, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal, said 148 containers had been sent out under the first phase of the operation.
He said that under the ongoing second phase, the agency, in collaboration with the Port Klang Authority and the Customs Department, had shipped out 255 of the 533 containers.
"For phase three, starting Oct 1, we will handle the remaining 578 containers, with the e-waste estimated at eight million kilogrammes, depending on ongoing investigations," he told reporters after a press conference at the Selangor Customs Department office here today.
Nik Ezanee added that all the containers involved had been detained since 2024.
He said that, to date, no containers containing e-waste that had been sent back had been detected re-entering the country, although some of the same containers had re-entered carrying other commercial goods.
"The Customs Department and MCBA have conducted inspections based on the recorded list, and those containers did not contain e-waste," he said.
Meanwhile, he gave assurances about the efficiency of the scanner machines at Port Klang.
"From time to time, we train our scanner officers to perform their duties effectively. I do not deny there are weaknesses, but I want to emphasise that we never stop improving our service," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US flags Malaysia in China tariff-evasion crackdown
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: US trade regulators have flagged Malaysia among more than 40 trade partners identified as risks for aiding tariff evasion, as Washington intensifies its global crackdown on China-linked transshipment networks.
In a report titled 'The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs,' the White House Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy (OTMP) named Malaysia alongside more than 40 countries accused of serving as conduits for illegal pass-through trade.
The document places Malaysia in Tier 2 as a 'scale leader with significant economic integration with China', warning that local deep-water ports, manufacturing hubs and free trade zones are being systematically exploited to cloak Chinese origin and bypass US Section 301 tariffs and anti-dumping duties.
This puts Malaysia in the same tier as Brazil, Indonesia, Thailand, Turkey and Vietnam.
According to the White House findings, global illicit rerouting costs Washington tens of billions of dollars annually in lost tariff revenue while displacing American domestic production.
Citing five government and private-sector economic models, the report estimates total annual illegal transshipment trade flows between US$40 billion (Goldman Sachs estimate) and US$303 billion (Altana estimate), with the Council of Economic Advisers using a US$60 billion midpoint baseline.
A US Commerce Department transaction-level analysis revealed that transshipment alone drains an estimated US$28 billion annually in uncollected customs revenue from the US Treasury while undercutting American industrial output.
The US report reveals that Malaysia performs a dual function within regional transshipment schemes, operating simultaneously as a production-side microhub and a logistics-side maritime gateway, including through the Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ).
"In their role as maritime gateways, deep-water ports, container relays, free-zone re-exports and re-invoicing facilities allow Chinese-origin goods to be passed off with new certificates of origin," read the report.
On the manufacturing front, the report said the Penang–Kulim industrial corridor was named as the 'ugly sister city', directly matching its output profile against impacted American manufacturing centres in Akron, Canton and Upstate South Carolina.
The 'ugly sister city' comparisons show how Chinese transshipment equates to a zero-sum transfer of production from American soil to foreign jurisdictions.
"The foreign–US city pairings reveal the micro-geography of trade diversion: as activity rises in foreign staging points handling China-linked goods, the corresponding American manufacturing corridors come under direct pressure."
Under this mapping methodology, Washington charges that rerouted plastic components (HS Code 392690) originating from Penang–Kulim directly displace US domestic capacity, undercutting American plastics fabricators and putting domestic jobs at risk.
Beyond industrial plastics, the report flags widespread circumvention of US Antidumping and Countervailing Duties (AD/CVD).
Malaysia, alongside regional neighbours Vietnam, Thailand and Cambodia, was specifically cited for active duty circumvention involving solar cells and modules (HS Code 8541).
"Solar cells and modules from China have likewise carried AD/CVD exposure well above 30 per cent, with later circumvention findings involving Chinese-origin inputs completed in Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam.
"These examples do not mean every illegally transshipped product carries AD/CVD exposure. They do, however, show that many AD/CVD-covered product categories overlap with the kinds of goods vulnerable to illegal transshipment: aluminium products, solar components, machinery inputs, industrial parts, household appliances and other manufactured goods," read the report.
The New Straits Times has reached out to the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry for comment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia to close more than 750 state-owned enterprises
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia's president mulled the possibility of a special court on Friday to investigate "unproductive" boards reporting "made up" profits, as he vowed to close 750 state-owned enterprises by year end.
Southeast Asia's biggest economy has long battled corruption in its public and private sectors despite strengthening anti-graft laws, creating special investigative commissions and arresting several high profile people.
"There are far too many unproductive state-owned enterprises, always reporting losses while claiming profits – those profits are just made up," Prabowo said in his state of the nation address to parliament.
With the establishment last year of Indonesia's Danantara sovereign wealth fund to manage state assets, "we discovered that there are 1,074 state-owned enterprises," the president told lawmakers.
"I had thought there were 300 or 400 state-owned enterprises, but it turns out there are 1,074. And these state-owned enterprises sometimes operate as they please, with no sense of responsibility to the nation, to the state."
So far, 290 have been closed, Prabowo added, and by December 31, there should be no more than 300 left.
"We will close more than 750 enterprises and retain only those that are productive, those that create added value for the people," the president added, in what "may be the largest corporate restructuring in the world."
The drive has already saved about 50 trillion rupiah (more than $2.8 billion) in overhead costs, including directors' and commissioners' salaries, building and car rentals and business travel, said Prabowo.
The target for this year was to save more than 70 trillion rupiah.
Thanks to "improvements" in how state-owned enterprises are managed, profits rose more than 75 per cent from 2024 to 326 trillion rupiah last year, the president said.
- 'Improvements and efficiency' -
Prabowo mooted the creation of "a special ad hoc court to investigate the management and boards" of state-owned enterprises "going back 30 years, maybe."
But he also asked lawmakers to consider a kind of "special amnesty for those who repent."
Indonesia scored a low 34 out of 100 on Amnesty International's Corruption Perceptions Index for 2025.
Graft has also been a rallying cry for protesters decrying rising living costs as Indonesia and the region reels from high oil prices caused by the Middle East war.
One project that comes in for particular criticism is the costly free school meals programme, Prabowo's signature project which he vowed Friday to pursue "but with improvements and efficiency."
"We cannot accept that one in four Indonesian children suffer from stunting," the president said.
Despite global uncertainty, Prabowo insisted the country was food and energy secure and said he was "confident" economic growth would reach 6.0 per cent by the end of 2026.
GDP came in at 5.3 per cent in the second quarter of the year, following on 5.6 per cent in the first, though analysts have repeatedly expressed scepticism about Indonesia's official growth data.
"Growth and investment are not the ultimate goal," Prabowo said Friday.
"Our goal is the prosperity of our people... Every rupiah of investment must create jobs and improve the quality of life of our people, especially those at the bottom."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 82,092 candidates offered undergraduate spots in 20 public universities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 82,092 candidates have been offered bachelor's degree placements at 20 public universities this year, according to the Higher Education Ministry (MoHE).
In a statement today, MoHE announced that the figure represents 76.10 per cent of the 107,875 applications eligible to pursue undergraduate studies via UPUOnline.
Overall, a total of 1,146 bachelor's degree programmes are offered for this session.
MoHE said student admissions to the institution are based on the principle of meritocracy by arranging all eligible candidates according to their merit scores from highest to lowest.
"The ministry extends its best wishes to all successful candidates and hopes that the opportunity to continue their studies at the higher education level will be utilised to the fullest," according to the statement.
For candidates who do not receive an offer for placement, they could submit an appeal on UPUOnline within a period of 10 days, starting from noon today until 5pm on Aug 23.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Law student fined RM500 for allowing account to be used in illegal transactions
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 22-year-old private college law student was fined RM500 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to allowing her bank account to be used for illegal transactions.
Judge Madihah Zainol ordered Nicole Soo Lik Yee to serve one month in jail if she fails to pay the fine.
Soo was charged with dishonestly transferring RM525 belonging to a 32-year-old man into her bank account at Jalan Idaman 8/10, Taman Nusa Idaman, Iskandar Puteri, at 4.31pm on June 13.
The charge was framed under Section 424 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of five years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
National Legal Aid Foundation counsel K. Bharathi, representing Soo, pleaded for a lenient sentence, saying the accused is studying law in Petaling Jaya and is dependent on her grandfather following her parents' separation.
Deputy public prosecutor Shamira Mohd Luthfi Ismail prosecuted.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: High chance of haze persisting until late September
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hazy conditions are expected to persist until late September, although the situation nationwide remains under control for now, says the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
Its director-general, Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, said current haze levels have not reached the extremes seen in previous episodes, except in Sarawak.
He said the situation in the state is expected to remain unchanged over the next few days.
Dry weather since late July has heightened the haze risk in Sarawak, compounded by transboundary smoke from West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
He said the situation would only improve if there was a drastic reduction in hotspots in West Kalimantan, as open burning is the primary cause of haze.
"Localised haze can also stem from vehicle and industrial emissions, particularly in industrial sectors and densely populated areas like the Klang Valley and Penang.
"With dry weather under the Southwest Monsoon expected to persist until late September, the likelihood of localised haze continuing through that period remains high," he said.
Hisham said that while the ongoing El Nino phenomenon is causing drier weather than usual, rainfall in parts of Peninsular Malaysia has provided relief.
He added that MetMalaysia stands ready to conduct cloud seeding operations if atmospheric conditions permit, noting that the process requires a moist atmosphere with active convective clouds to generate rain.
As of 2.20pm today, 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality, with the majority in Sarawak.
Data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Serian registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 182, followed by Kuching (170), Samarahan (169), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (158), Mukah (151), Bintulu (151), and Sibu (104).
In Peninsular Malaysia, two areas recorded unhealthy readings: Cheras (153) and Johan Setia (135).

Title: Farage wins UK by-election as Count Binface claims 'moral victory'
Article:
CLACTON-ON-SEA, United Kingdom: Hard-right British politician Nigel Farage reclaimed his seat in a by-election, according to the final tally Friday, though his main rival and joke candidate Count Binface took an larger than expected share of the ballot.
Farage, who triggered the vote by resigning the parliamentary seat he had held since 2024 over an investigation into his finances, swept 63 per cent of the ballots in the English constituency of Clacton.
While votes were still being counted, Farage had declared victory.
"The verdict is in and it is a convincing and overwhelming win," he said as supporters chanted his name at an event in Essex that was broadcast on X.
His main rival, Count Binface, however, exceeded expectations by earning 9,455 votes, 27 percent of the total.
Analysts had anticipated a win for Farage but underestimated the appeal of the self-styled "intergalactic space warrior", who campaigns wearing a rubbish bin on his head, forecasting a large share of the vote approaching but not exceeding 20 per cent.
The vote had been shunned by Britain's main political parties, including the governing Labour Party, as a stunt by the Reform UK leader – once touted as a potential prime minister – to dodge scrutiny of his dealings.
That gave dozens of fringe candidates including Binface – the alter ego of comedian Jon Harvey – to seize the spotlight.
"The moral victory is already mine," he told AFP at the counting centre early Friday ahead of the final tally.
Farage did not attend the count, where candidates traditionally gather for the declaration of results, saying Essex Police had warned him that an "organised campaign to disrupt and degrade the result" was planned.
Acting Returning Officer Ian Davidson said election officials had worked with police to ensure the process was "completed safely and securely", adding there was "no reason not to proceed with the count process at this time."
Binface said it had been his "humble duty" to be Farage's opposition, adding he would respect the results.
"If a majority of the voters of Clacton say they would like him to be returned as their MP, that is to be respected," he said.
Turnout reached about 44 per cent, down from 59 per cent in the 2024 general election but not an unusual rate for a by-election.
In the coastal community, many voters appeared unenthusiastic about the vote, with even some Reform party volunteers describing the contest as a joke.
"It's a bit ridiculous," party campaigner Jane Embelton told AFP.
"It's all to make Nigel Farage look like an idiot, basically. But he doesn't look like an idiot to me or his supporters."
A record 33 fringe candidates, including Binface, stood in the vote, with some of the longest ballot papers in the country's history seen being unfolded at the Clacton Leisure Centre, where the count was held.
- 'WE CAN'T DECIDE' -
Farage, whose party had topped national opinion polls for 18 months before falling behind recently, surprised voters with his July 7 resignation amid the probe into his finances.
The investigation by the parliamentary sleaze watchdog is examining allegations he and Reform's deputy leader, Richard Tice, failed to declare financial gifts. They deny any wrongdoing.
Farage has framed Thursday's vote as "the people of Clacton versus the Establishment", aimed at thwarting the "stitch-up" over his finances.
"The people of Clacton should be the judges of my actions," he said in a video released before casting his vote.
One Clacton voter, Phil, predicted the vote was "not going to change anything", saying that the parliamentary probe would restart with Farage's re-election.
Political pundits have downplayed the vote's wider significance in a constituency that overwhelmingly backed Brexit a decade ago.
"It will be astonishing if Farage were not to win," political scientist John Curtice told AFP.
But some assessed Farage's election gambit had backfired as his Reform party slips down national polls.
"Farage's plan to turn this by-election into a serious political battle failed," Queen Mary University of London politics professor Stijn van Kessel told AFP, noting the resulting spectacle "makes Farage look rather silly."
Farage netted 46 per cent of the vote in the 2024 general election to become an MP on his eighth attempt.
- POLICE PROBE -
The probe into Farage, which paused when he resigned, relates to a five million pound (US$6.7 million) donation from the cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne.
Meanwhile, London police have confirmed starting a investigation last year into donations to Reform before the 2024 election.
UK media have reported that probe concerns undeclared financial support from longtime Farage ally and convicted fraudster George Cottrell and his mother.
The controversies have coincided with the drop in Reform polling support and in popularity for Farage, long a divisive figure loved and loathed in largely equal measure.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Toyo Tyre puts Malaysia at heart of growth push
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Toyo Tyre is putting its Malaysian manufacturing operations at the centre of its growth strategy, combining local production capabilities with Japanese engineering as it seeks to strengthen its position in an increasingly competitive tyre market.
The Japanese tyre maker recently unveiled its new brand manifesto, "Buatan Malaysia, Keunggulan Jepun", positioning Malaysian manufacturing and Japanese technology as key differentiators while seeking to make premium-quality tyres more accessible to local motorists.
The strategy goes beyond product quality, with Toyo Tires focusing on manufacturing efficiency, digitalisation and stronger relationships with consumers and business partners.
Toyo Tyre Malaysia president and managing director Mike Toh said its Taiping plant is advancing its intelligent manufacturing transformation (IMX) programme to create a smarter, more efficient and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem.
"Our Taiping factory is also advancing its IMX journey to create a smarter, more efficient and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem," Toh said in a launch.
The company said its Malaysian factory is staffed entirely by local workers, with the manufacturing operation supporting local employment while developing capabilities in advanced tyre production.
The combination of local manufacturing and Japanese technology is also aimed at reinforcing Toyo Tyre's role as an original equipment (OE) supplier to leading automotive manufacturers.
Toyo Tyre Sales and Marketing Malaysia Sdn Bhd president and managing director Tan Song Chye said the company's competitive proposition was built around combining local craftsmanship with Japanese precision.
"We are the only tyre manufacturer in Malaysia combining the local craftsmanship with Japanese precision to achieve the premium-quality standards" he said.
Founded in Osaka in 1945, Toyo Tyre brings more than eight decades of Japanese engineering experience to its Malaysian operations, including the kaizen philosophy of continuous improvement.
The company said this manufacturing model allows it to offer Japanese-quality tyres at prices that are more accessible to Malaysian consumers, while maintaining its focus on safety, reliability and value.
"A great product deserves a great experience. We want to continue caring for motorists beyond their tyre purchase, while giving our business partners the tools to grow. Through technology, we can stay connected and closer to those who trust our brand," Tan said.
Beyond its commercial ambitions, Toyo Tyre is also stepping up its community commitments through its Komuniti Prihatin Toyo initiative.
The company contributed RM30,000 to the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund, reinforcing its focus on community welfare alongside business growth.
The fund provides assistance to underprivileged Malaysians requiring life-saving medical treatment and surgery, while extending support to other vulnerable groups.
In the 2026 financial year, the Media Prima-NSTP Humanitarian Fund assisted 143 Malaysians in accessing medical treatment and provided aid to underprivileged communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai schools tighten security after deadly shooting
Article:
BANGKOK: Students stood quietly outside their Bangkok school Friday as teachers checked their bags, pockets and even pencil cases under new security measures introduced after last week's deadly shooting.
Thailand's government has ordered schools nationwide to step up controls following the August 7 attack near Bangkok, when a 14-year-old killed his grandparents, five school staff and a pupil before turning the gun on himself.
"An incident like this should not have happened in a school," headteacher Suparong Sawangngamwong told AFP after overseeing the new checks at Bangkok's Sawasdee Wittaya School.
He said he hoped the inspections will ensure "parents can be at ease", assuring them school is a safe place "where parents trust their children can spend their days."
A modest public school nestled among the city's affluent neighbourhoods, Sawasdee Wittaya has more than 500 pupils aged six to 12, and 30 teachers.
Six teachers on Friday morning meticulously searched pupils' backpacks as they arrived for class, going through every pocket.
As they returned the bags, the children, one by one, pressed their palms together and bowed to the teachers in the Thai greeting taught as part of school etiquette.
Previously, "we would only randomly check the bags of students in the higher grades, or kids with problematic behaviour", said Suparong, who has more than two decades of teaching experience.
"But now we do it for everyone."
- 'SAFE ZONE' -
The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) this week ordered schools under its authority to screen for weapons, maintain around-the-clock security and enforce strict protocols for visitors.
The measures have been welcomed by some parents.
"The school should be a safe zone for kids," said Araya Chanu as she dropped off her daughter in the fifth grade (aged 10 or 11).
The 37-year-old said last Friday's shooting in Nonthaburi, not far away on the outskirts of the Thai capital, had left her worried.
But she told AFP the new measures would help, adding: "If parents work together with the school, I think it will become more efficient."
The school already works with local police to conduct emergency drills once every term, Suparong added.
Two security guards and six teachers are also on duty each day, rotating shifts to ensure that every child is safely collected by their parents.
But Suparong warned his school needed more funding to make the changes required.
There are CCTV cameras across the school's four floors, but some are out of order and more are needed, he said.
In last Friday's shooting, the assailant used his grandfather's gun to kill his grandparents before heading to his school.
There, he shot dead five teachers and staff and wounded a 12-year-old girl, who died in hospital the following day.
The incident revived debate over firearms control in Thailand, which has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region.
In the wake of the attack, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul ordered the interior ministry and police to stop issuing licenses to possess, purchase and carry firearms, and called for "tighter controls and decisive penalties."
However, past promises of tightening gun laws have not prevented repeated shootings.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Higher-quality investments may take time to lift wages, household incomes: Bank Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's efforts to attract higher-quality investments and move up the value chain could eventually translate into higher wages and household incomes, although the benefits may take time to filter through the economy.
Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said stronger economic growth did not immediately translate into higher household incomes as there was usually a time lag before the benefits reached the population.
"We may not feel it immediately, but given what we're seeing in terms of our growth right now and the quality of investment that we're attracting right now, which creates higher income jobs.
"Slowly this will pass through into the income of the population as well," he told reporters at a press conference following the release of Malaysia's second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data today.
Abdul Rasheed said the country needed to continue attracting quality investments, moving up the value chain and improving productivity to support higher wages and incomes.
He said these measures would ultimately help improve the livelihoods of the population while supporting the economy.
Abdul Rasheed said foreign investment inflows continued to be channelled towards high-value-added activities in the manufacturing and services sectors, particularly electrical and electronics (E&E), chemicals and information and communications technology (ICT) services.
He said investment activity continued to be supported by foreign investments and a steady pipeline of newly approved projects.
As of June, 85 per cent of manufacturing projects approved between 2021 and February 2026 had progressed to implementation, ranging from factory construction to production and machinery installation.
Statistics Department chief statistician Siti Asiah Ahmad said foreign direct investment (FDI) recorded a net inflow of RM7.4 billion in the second quarter, bringing total FDI inflows in the first half of 2026 to RM30.2 billion.
The Q2 inflows were supported by higher equity capital injections from abroad and reinvestment of earnings by foreign-owned companies in Malaysia, she said.
"However, the inflows were partially offset by outflows in debt instruments arising from intercompany loans and trade credit activities.
"This FDI was channelled largely into the services sector, mainly in ICT and professional and technical sub-sectors, and this FDI was mostly from China, Hong Kong and Singapore," Siti Asiah added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bank Negara approves RM2.8bil financing under SME relief facility
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has approved about RM2.8 billion in financing under its SME Stabilisation Relief Facility (SME SRF), benefiting more than 4,900 small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) accounts affected by the Middle East conflict.
Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the facility was introduced to provide working capital support to viable businesses, including microentrepreneurs, to sustain operations amid economic disruptions arising from the conflict.
"While the immediate focus is on short-term stabilisation, we must not lose sight of longer-term resilience," he said.
The RM5 billion SME SRF was introduced by the central bank on April 28 to assist micro, SMEs affected by the ongoing Middle East conflict.
The facility remains open for applications until the end of this year or until the allocation is fully utilised.
Abdul Rasheed said structural improvements to the financing ecosystem were also important to help SMEs withstand future shocks, seize new opportunities and grow into domestic champions.
To support this, Bank Negara has introduced a RM10 billion guarantee scheme through Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC).
He said the scheme was aimed at mobilising private sector financing more effectively, with a focus on financial inclusion, climate, productivity and resilience.
On overall financing conditions, Abdul Rasheed said they remained supportive, with credit continuing to flow to businesses despite external uncertainties.
"On aggregate, credit growth to the private non-financial sector increased to 6.4 per cent (1Q 2026: 5.6 per cent), particularly among the business segment," he said.
Corporate bonds expanded 8.1 per cent in the second quarter, compared with 5.9 per cent in the first quarter, amid higher issuances for working capital needs.
Business loan growth also strengthened to 7.2 per cent from 5.7 per cent previously, supported by sustained disbursements across business segments.
Household loan growth, meanwhile, remained broadly stable at 5.4 per cent during the quarter, compared with 5.5 per cent in the first quarter.
Abdul Rasheed said financing conditions for SMEs also remained healthy, with outstanding SME financing growing 4.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2026.
"Financing activity remained supported by higher financing approvals, particularly for investment-related purposes.
"Approval rates continued to be sustained, as banks continue to meet financing demand across all sectors, particularly in agriculture, mining and quarrying, and construction," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KJ says new Tabung Haji RCI premature
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin says it is premature to establish a new Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji.
He said a detailed management report or audit should first determine why the fund's asset recovery plan had fallen short.
Speaking on the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, Khairy said the underperformance of assets transferred to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) did not, by itself, justify another RCI, as it remained unclear whether the assets were unrecoverable or the recovery plan had failed.
"It's premature to call for an RCI.
"You can ask for a detailed management report or audit about what is happening to the assets under UJSB," he said.
Khairy said such an assessment could establish whether the assets were already too weak to recover or whether the recovery plan had simply failed in its execution.
"If the assets are indeed so bad they can't be recovered, or the plan for asset recovery simply didn't work as planned, then, at the moment on paper, it would not be a misappropriation issue. It's more an issue of execution based on the plan," he said.
Earlier, several BN and PH members of Parliament had called
for a new RCI
into Tabung Haji's management and operations, covering the 2021 to 2025 period during the Dewan Rakyat debate on the TH RCI report on Aug 11.
Meanwhile, Khairy also rejected suggestions that the issue pointed to misappropriation, saying the available evidence instead suggested weaknesses in management, governance and investment decisions.
"I don't see any 'sakau' here. I do see serious weaknesses in governance and in investment decisions for sure," he said.
Earlier, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said 14 investments identified by the RCI had resulted in estimated losses of nearly RM13 billion, including RM10.2 billion through the government's
2018 bailout
via UJSB and RM2.6 billion in impairments or net losses borne by Tabung Haji between 2018 and 2025.
Khairy added that Tabung Haji remained "not out of the woods" and that the effectiveness of measures taken after 2018 still needed to be examined.
Opposition MPs
staged a walkout
from the Dewan Rakyat on Tuesday after the Speaker rejected their call to postpone the special sitting on the RCI report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stop dwelling on losses, focus on way forward, says Fadhlina
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR leaders and members must stop dwelling on Pakatan Harapan's (PH) recent electoral defeats and focus on the way forward.
PKR Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek said after the conclusion of the PKR congress on Sunday, the wing must go down to the ground, activate initiatives and engage with women.
"We must knock on every door. Reclaim our role at the grassroots level as voices for women, and focus on female voters.
"The 'Dapur Wanita' (initiative) is the most crucial place to carry out political work.
"Start with the 'Dapur Wanita'. Ask them if there is rice today, whether there is enough sugar and salt, and how many times a day the children eat," she said in her speech at the PKR Wanita congress.
She said upcoming state elections, particularly in Melaka and Sarawak, were vital to ensuring the party's survival ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
"Melaka is very important to us. We must execute the same machinery and deploy all our best field commanders. Continue training, as Sarawak is coming. We must organise now.
"When we reflect on our past election losses, we know how it felt—sad and angry. Therefore, we must strengthen our organisation, fortify election training, and win over women across Malaysia," she said.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina said the party must provide more opportunities for women to be fielded as election candidates.
"When entering elections, we must field female candidates. Whatever the challenges, female candidates must be included. I want 30 per cent women candidates. We must defend this 30 per cent quota.
"Now is the time to feature leaders who meet the criteria to become election candidates. We must prepare them and highlight them," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police identify drug syndicate links in Malaysian pilot's case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian narcotics investigators have obtained crucial information how the Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested with drugs in Jakarta managed to clear security checks at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had also uncovered information on the local and international drug syndicates linked to the case, including individuals believed to be part of their networks.
He, however, did not disclose how the pilot beat security at KLIA saying that the matter is still under investigation.
He said the developments followed two days of questioning of the 39-year-old pilot in Jakarta on Aug 12 and 13.
"The meetings over the first two days enabled the NCID team to identify the syndicates involved in Malaysia and overseas, as well as individuals involved in the domestic and international drug networks.
"We also obtained information how the suspect managed to get through checks at KLIA, as well as the financial flows of the drug syndicates in Malaysia and abroad," he said.
Hussein said the four-member NCID team had received good cooperation from the Indonesian National Police (Polri), which facilitated access to the suspect.
He said the pilot had also cooperated well with Malaysian investigators during the questioning sessions.
The Malaysian team was initially scheduled to meet and question the pilot on Aug 12 and 13.
However, Hussein said Polri had allowed the questioning to be extended for another day, until today (Aug 14), following the progress made during the first two days.
"The meetings have produced significant results for NCID in several areas.
"Among them is assisting us in tracking down members of the drug syndicate involved in Malaysia," he said.
Hussein said information obtained from the pilot would also be channelled to drug enforcement agencies in countries linked to the international network.
He said this would allow foreign authorities to act on intelligence concerning members and operations of the syndicate outside Malaysia.
"The latest breakthrough could provide investigators with new leads in determining the full network behind the drugs allegedly carried by the pilot and how the consignment was able to leave Malaysia," he said.
The pilot was arrested by Indonesian authorities at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28 after arriving from Kuala Lumpur.
Indonesian authorities reportedly seized 15 packets containing about 70,000 capsules suspected to contain ecstasy and methamphetamine, weighing about 25kg and estimated to be worth RM45 million.
Police are also investigating a telephone number allegedly used by the syndicate to communicate with the pilot, which is believed to have been registered using false particulars.
Investigators have also recorded a statement from KLIA personnel as part of the probe, although police have said it remains too early to establish or rule out the involvement of any airport personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two face conspiracy charges over alleged healing scam
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Two women arrested recently over an alleged traditional healing scam were charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of criminal conspiracy to cheat three women.
Malaysian Hee Nyin Fung, 48, and Chinese national Li Li, 38, pleaded not guilty to two charges before judge Zaini Fishir @ Fisal and another before judge Monica Linsua after the charges were read to them in Mandarin.
They were accused of engaging in a criminal conspiracy by agreeing to commit an unlawful act, namely to cheat three local women, an offence contrary to Section 420 of the Penal Code.
On the first charge, Hee, a businesswoman, and Li, a company director, allegedly conspired to cheat a 51-year-old woman at the Kota Kinabalu Central Market at 7.30am on Feb 4.
The second charge involved a 69-year-old woman at the Gaya Street Sunday Market here at 11.30am on July 19.
The third charge involved a 45-year-old woman at the Manggatal Town Market here at 8am on Feb 3.
They were charged under Section 120B(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
The court fixed Oct 1 for pre-trial case management and allowed each accused bail of RM5,000 with a RM2,000 deposit for each charge and two local sureties.
They were also ordered to report to the nearest police station once a month, surrender their passports to the court and not contact, communicate with or harass any prosecution witnesses.
Lawyer Batholomew Jingulam represented Hee, while Muhamad Amirul Amin represented Li.
Deputy public prosecutors Mohd Fadzri Azham Zainudin and Nurul Shaferrah Mad Iskim prosecuted the cases before judge Zaini and judge Monica, respectively.
On Thursday, media reports said police have crippled a
syndicate that duped victims
of about RM600,000 by offering fortune-telling and ritual cleansing services to remove bad luck.
Twelve individuals, including seven Chinese citizens, were arrested in several raids in Kota Kinabalu, Penampang, Keningau and Kota Belud.
The syndicate, which had been active since early this year, would approach victims and offer traditional remedies, treatment for illnesses or religious rituals to cleanse bad luck.
The victims would then be persuaded to hand over cash or jewellery, purportedly for prayers, rituals or blessings, before the valuables were taken away or replaced with other items.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lim Guan Eng hits back at Chow over Penang PH-Umno cooperation
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow over the coalition's decision to work with Umno.
Lim said Chow appeared to be confused when he claimed that no objection had been raised to Penang PH's decision to accept Umno's role in the state government during a DAP Penang delegates' gathering on Wednesday.
"Chow must be confused when he said that at the Penang DAP's delegates gathering attended by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke on Wednesday night, neither I nor anyone raised any objection to Penang PH's decision to work and accept Umno's role in the Penang state government," he said in a statement.
Lim said he had questioned last week why Penang PH's political leadership had failed to act decisively against what he described as baseless attacks by Penang Umno accusing DAP and PKR of playing identity politics.
He said the issue was not raised at Wednesday's meeting because its sole agenda was whether DAP should remain in or leave the federal government, rather than discussing Umno's role in the Penang state administration.
Lim said only Loke, among the senior central executive committee (CEC) leaders present, spoke during the meeting, explaining the current political scenario and responding to delegates' questions on the advantages and disadvantages of remaining in the federal government.
He also said neither Chow nor any other national CEC leader addressed the delegates.
"As a veteran CEC leader, Chow should not be discussing the internal details of this closed-door party meeting," Lim said, adding that only the DAP secretary-general had the prerogative to comment on the proceedings.
Lim said Chow had every right to maintain his decision to continue working with Umno, despite Umno's alleged role in Loke's defeat in the Chennah state seat during the Negri Sembilan state election.
However, he said Chow should not assume Penang DAP delegates endorsed the decision simply because the issue was not raised at Wednesday's meeting.
Lim suggested that Chow call another internal DAP Penang delegates' meeting to gauge their views on Penang PH's endorsement of Umno's role in the state government.
He said such a meeting could also consider whether the approach would send a message that Penang's political leadership was prepared to defend its honour and dignity as the state government and elected representatives.
Yesterday, Chow said Penang PH remains committed to its decision to accept Barisan Nasional and Umno despite criticism from Lim.
Chow said the
decision was not questioned
during a recent engagement session involving the state coalition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM Anwar hails stronger Q2 expansion, says govt shielded households from global inflation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today welcomed Malaysia’s stronger than expected second quarter growth, saying the 6 per cent expansion underscored the government’s efforts to shield households from global inflationary pressures.
In a Facebook post, Anwar described the second quarter growth as the country’s strongest performance outside the pandemic period since 2014, despite global supply disruptions and conflict in West Asia.
“This strength was made possible by the Madani government’s efforts to ensure the people’s lives were not severely affected by global inflationary pressures,” he said.
He cited initiatives such as Budi Madani, Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), alongside behind the scenes measures to stabilise prices and maintain supply.
Anwar acknowledged that more work remained to sustain growth and ensure its benefits were widely shared. “We must guarantee meaningful incomes, quality job opportunities and assistance for vulnerable groups,” he said.
He added that the government would remain committed to reforms aimed at strengthening the economy and uplifting the people. “Insya Allah, the Madani government will stay on the reform path to raise the dignity of the people and reinforce the foundations of our beloved nation’s economy,” he said.

Title: Lim Guan Eng rebukes Penang CM Chow, disputes claim DAP delegates endorsed Umno partnership
Article:
