GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Lim Guan Eng has clarified that Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to work with Umno in the state government was not discussed at last week’s Penang DAP delegates’ meeting.
Lim said the meeting, attended by current secretary general Loke Siew Fook, focused solely on whether DAP should remain in the federal government, and not on Umno’s role in Penang.
He stressed that neither he nor any delegate raised the matter, as the agenda was confined to debating the pros and cons of staying in Putrajaya.
“However Chow should not presume that all Penang delegates endorsed his decision merely because no one raised it at Wednesday’s meeting when the Penang DAP delegates were focused on whether to stay or leave the Federal government in Putrajaya,” Lim said.
He criticised Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow for commenting publicly on internal party discussions, saying only the secretary general had the prerogative to do so.
Lim added that Chow was entitled to continue working with Umno despite the party’s role in defeating Loke in Negeri Sembilan’s Chennah seat, but cautioned against assuming Penang delegates had endorsed the decision.
Lim’s remarks came a day after Chow said Penang PH was sticking with its decision to continue working with Barisan Nasional (BN), including Umno, despite Lim’s criticism.
Chow told reporters yesterday that the decision remained Penang PH’s position and was not challenged during the state DAP engagement session, adding that “no one questioned it”.

Title: Hop on, KK: BAS.MY pink buses expand eight routes, easing commutes across the city
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — After four months of operation on its initial two routes, Kota Kinabalu’s new fixed-schedule BAS.MY “pink bus” service is now running across all eight routes, giving commuters more options for getting around the city and surrounding areas.
The full rollout of routes S01 to S08 began last Tuesday, completing the phased introduction of the service that started on April 1 with routes S01 and S05.
The first two routes have already recorded strong demand, with 194,265 passengers using the service between April 1 and August 10.
The figure is expected to increase with the addition of the six remaining routes — S02, S03, S04, S06, S07 and S08.
The expanded network is intended to make public transport a more practical option for daily travel, particularly for residents who do not own cars or motorcycles.
Buses now operate from 5.30am to 11pm daily, with services running at intervals of between 15 and 30 minutes.
A total of 48 new buses has been deployed to connect the main hubs at KK Sentral and Menggatal with the eight routes.
The service also offers free concession cards to students, senior citizens and persons with disabilities (OKU), with 960 people registered so far.
For commuters who depend on public transport, the concession scheme could help reduce the cost of daily travel, while the expanded network provides greater connectivity between residential areas and key destinations.
The buses are also equipped with real-time GPS monitoring, allowing their movements to be tracked, as well as cashless payment and e-ticketing systems.
Safety and accessibility features include closed-circuit television cameras and designs aimed at making the buses more accessible to senior citizens and persons with disabilities.
The full operation of BAS.MY Kota Kinabalu is part of the Federal Government’s Stage Bus Service Transformation (SBST) programme implemented through the Transport Ministry.
The programme involves an allocation of RM17.6 million a year, or RM88 million over five years.
Earlier this year, civil society group Sabah Entitlement and Equity Now (SEEN) and Api-Api assemblyman Loi Kok Liang raised questions about the fleet procurement of the buses.
The Sabah Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) subsequently defended the process, saying operator Jaguh Bayu Sdn Bhd was selected through the government’s ePerolehan system following technical and financial evaluations. LPKP also said the use of smaller buses was intended to suit Kota Kinabalu’s narrower roads and existing bus stops.
There were also concerns during the early rollout that awareness of BAS.MY remained low, with Kota Kinabalu MP Chan Foong Hin previously urging wider publicity to familiarise residents with the new service.

Title: From FOMO to future jobs: PKR Youth motions put Gen Z outreach in focus
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Youth issues took centre stage at the 2026 National Congress of Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) today, with motions focusing on stronger engagement with Generation Z (Gen Z), jobs of the future, mental health and social wellbeing.
Three delegates from Perak, Terengganu and Sarawak called on PKR to refine its approach to better reflect the realities and needs of young Malaysians.
Syahnaz Putera Mohd Yaacob, who is Perak AMK Information chief, said PKR faced challenges in winning support from younger voters, particularly Gen Z.
He said the party needs a bolder and more creative approach to engage Gen Z, particularly through digital platforms, while helping them develop their talents and gain access to government opportunities and funding.
“It is a bitter reality we have to accept. Gen Z cast their votes simply because of FOMO, the fear of missing out. When their friends voted and flexed their inked fingers, so they vote too,” he said while tabling the motion.
Syahnaz also suggested helping young people register clubs and associations, giving them formal entities through which they could apply for funding and develop their talents.
Meanwhile, Terengganu AMK chief Md Asyraf Zulfadhly Md Zainudin tabled a motion on future jobs and the gig economy, aimed at expanding income opportunities for young people.
He proposed four measures, namely recognising the gig economy as an employment sector with comprehensive social protection; providing gig workers with pathways to upgrade their skills; expanding upskilling and reskilling programmes; and strengthening links between universities, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions, and industry.
Separately, Christopher Jemat Amie, who is Sarawak AMK secretary, highlighted mental health and social wellbeing as key areas that should receive sustained attention under the reform agenda.
He urged the PKR leadership to make mental health and social wellbeing a continuing priority rather than an issue addressed only after tragedies.
“Make mental health and social wellbeing part of the reform agenda. It should not be seasonal or addressed only when tragedy strikes, but pursued continuously,” he said.
“We do not only want to build an advanced nation. We want to build a nation whose people progress as well,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two women in dock for allegedly duping retiree in Perak out of RM120,000 over fake tax arrears
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — Two women were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with three counts of cheating a male retiree of about RM120,000 by falsely claiming they could help him settle his tax arrears.
Noorfarah Surina Ahmad, 42, and Nurfalah Noordin, 33, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Magistrate S. Punitha.
The two women allegedly cheated Koay Kuang Hew, 60, by offering to help him settle his tax arrears, which actually did not exist, thereby dishonestly inducing Koay to give them the money, made in three transactions on April 10 and 14 and June 4 this year.
The offences were allegedly committed at Wisma Hasil, Jalan Tambun, in the Kinta district.
They were charged under Section 420 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 10 years, a fine and whipping upon conviction.
Magistrate Punitha set bail at RM4,500 with one surety for each accused and set Sept 24 for mention.
Both accused were also ordered to report to the nearest police station once a month pending disposal of the case.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Zarris Sofea Zainudin appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Izzat Fakhri Halimi and Intan Shafini Mior Shahrin represented Noorfarah Surina and Nurfalah, respectively. — Bernama

Title: ‘Datuk Seri’ businessman claims trial to RM37.1m company funds breach of trust at Bukit Tunku bank
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — A businessman with a “Datuk Seri” title pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.1 million in company funds, allegedly committed four years ago.
Datuk Seri Zul Azmi Abu Hussin, 51, a director of Xspec Resources Sdn Bhd, was accused of misappropriating RM37,099,999.67 in company funds at a bank in Taman Tunku, Bukit Tunku here on Feb 15, 2022.
The charge was brought under Section 409 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment, caning and a fine, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Suriatey Mohamed Yusoff applied for bail of RM500,000 with one surety, along with an additional condition that the accused surrender his passport to the court until the case is concluded.
Zul Azmi’s lawyer Edly Mohammad Firdaus, however, applied for bail at RM50,000, citing that his client supports a wife, five children and elderly parents, and suffers from hypertension.
“My client was called in to give a statement today before being charged. He has fully cooperated with the investigation. Bail is not a form of early punishment, but to ensure the accused’s presence in court,” he submitted.
Judge Mohd Kafli Che Ali set bail at RM100,000 with one surety, along with the additional conditions sought by the prosecution, and fixed Oct 5 for case mention. — Bernama

Title: Illegal e-waste gets one-way ticket home as Malaysia targets 1,259 containers
Article:
PORT KLANG, Aug 14 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) aims to return all 1,259 containers of illegal electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin by year-end.
AKPS Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation is being conducted in three phases of integrated enforcement, involving about 8,000 metric tonnes of seized e-waste over the past two years in collaboration with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and Port Klang Authority.
“To date, we have shipped out 255 containers. We are now in the second phase, targeting the return of 533 containers of illegal e-waste.
“The third and final phase will begin on Oct 1, targeting the remaining 578 containers. The overall target of 1,259 containers is subject to any containers still under investigation,” he told reporters at the North Port Customs building here today.
Nik Ezanee said inspections have found no attempts to re-import the banned materials, though some containers have been detected returning with other commercial goods based on authority checklist reviews.
He said scanning machines at Port Klang remain highly efficient in detecting illegal shipments, but human weaknesses in their operation still pose challenges.
He acknowledged that there are occasional gaps, but said the agency continuously trains scanning officers to perform their duties well, and AKPS never stops improving its services.
On a related note, Nik Ezanee said the large-scale operation to return illegal e-waste reinforces the government’s commitment to ensuring Malaysian ports are not used as transit points or dumping grounds for toxic waste.
He said AKPS and other enforcement agencies remain committed to tightening risk profiling and taking stern legal action against any party attempting to violate laws and international conventions. — Bernama

Title: Three fight for one spot as vocational college applications surge past 67,000
Article:
TAIPING, Aug 14 — Applications for admission to Ministry of Education (MOE) Vocational Colleges (KV) have reached 67,045 nationwide as of today, against a capacity of 19,567 places.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the figure was expected to exceed 68,000 when applications close at midnight tonight.
He said this reflected strong interest in skills-based education, which was also reflected in the nearly 100 per cent employability rate recorded among KV graduates.
“The increase in applications proves the success of efforts by the Madani Government and the MOE to strengthen the TVET sector and subsequently boost graduate employability,” he told reporters after the signing ceremony for a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Toyo Tyre Malaysia Sdn Bhd and Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) here today.
Wong said the employability rate of KV graduates reached 99.95 per cent in 2023, while rates of between 98 and 99 per cent had been consistently recorded in recent years.
He said close collaboration between the MOE and industry players ensured that the fields offered and skills acquired by KV students met job market requirements.
“This exceptionally high employability rate shows that collaboration with industry is vital to ensure the fields offered and skills acquired meet job market requirements,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Eighteen lives lost daily is tough to stomach, but Works Ministry data is finally pointing to the fix
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 14 — The use of the Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Ministry of Works (KKR) to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur or ‘blackspots’ on federal roads nationwide.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by KKR under the MYJalan initiative, plays a role in systematically managing, analysing and displaying road accident data, including identifying locations where accidents frequently occur.
“The average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure,” he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here, today.
He said through the integration of accident data from the Integrated Police Reporting System (IPRS) under the supervision of the police, RAMS enables the planning and implementation of road safety interventions to be made more accurately and quickly.
“Accurate and quality data is an important basis in planning safer, more efficient and sustainable road infrastructure,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Mertajam Hospital makes global green list, ranks among world’s top 250
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 14 — Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) here has made history by being ranked among the 250 greenest hospitals in the world in the World’s Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking by Newsweek and Statista.
The Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement recognised HBM’s commitment to implementing climate-friendly healthcare practices and environmental sustainability.
“More importantly, HBM was selected, beating thousands of other hospitals from 36 countries in this inaugural edition, which recognises healthcare institutions worldwide for their outstanding commitment to climate-friendly healthcare and environmental sustainability.
“This proves that the sustainable healthcare agenda at MOH is not merely a campaign, but a real and continuous effort to build hospitals that are greener, more efficient and future-ready,” MOH said in a post on its Facebook page today.
MOH also congratulated the entire HBM staff and the MOH Engineering Services Division, which were instrumental in the hospital’s sustainability achievement. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman say they know how Malaysia Airlines pilot cleared KLIA checks after three-day interrogation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Police are pursuing members of a drug syndicate in Malaysia after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta late last month with more than 26 kilogrammes of drugs in his luggage.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the operation followed intelligence obtained after investigators interrogated the pilot over two days.
He said the questioning enabled police to gather information on syndicate networks in Malaysia and abroad, as well as the individuals involved. Hussein added that further details could not yet be disclosed publicly.
He said NCID had received strong cooperation from the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) during the investigation. The questioning, initially scheduled for August 12 and 13, was extended until August 14, and the pilot was reported to have given full cooperation.
Hussein said the investigation also allowed NCID to share key intelligence on international drug syndicates with relevant agencies.
“The team also learned how the suspect bypassed checks at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and about the syndicate’s financial flows at home and abroad,” he told BH.
The case involves a 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot who was arrested shortly after arriving at Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta International Airport from Kuala Lumpur on July 28.
Indonesian authorities said more than 26kg of ecstasy tablets and a packet of methamphetamine were found in a suitcase the pilot collected after customs officers flagged it during an X-ray inspection.

Title: Married couple plead guilty to causing death of three-month-old baby under their care in Johor
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — A husband and wife were charged in the Sessions Court here today with causing the death of a three-month-old baby boy who was under their care in Masai last month.
The accused, Mohd Iqbal Hassan, 36, and his wife, Norsiayana Abd Samad, 34, pleaded guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim.
According to the charge sheet, the couple, as persons having custody of Muhammad Saif Mohamad Sidiq, exposed the baby in a manner likely to cause him physical injury, resulting in his death.
The offence was allegedly committed at 1.03pm at a house in Jalan Cendana 21, Taman Rinting, Masai, on July 29.
They were charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both upon conviction.
The charge was read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which deals with joint liability.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shamira Mohd Luthfi Ismail prosecuted, while the couple were represented by K. Bharathi of the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK).
During the proceedings, Bharathi requested minimum bail for his clients.
He said Mohd Iqbal, a factory worker, earns RM3,000 a month, while Norsiayana earns RM2,000 as a nanny, and that the couple have a four-year-old child.
The court granted bail of RM7,000 to each accused and ordered them to report to the nearest police station once a month and surrender their passports to the court.
They were also prohibited from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
The court set September 17 for the presentation of the facts of the case and sentencing.

Title: ECRL Kota Bharu–Gombak service targets December 2026 launch, a month ahead of schedule
Article:
GOMBAK, Aug 14 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Phase 1 service from Kota Bharu to Gombak is targeted to commence operations as early as December, earlier than the original schedule in January 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the target depends on the smoothness of the ongoing testing and commissioning processes, including the System Integration Testing (SIT) and Fault-Free Run (FFR), without any compromise on safety aspects.
He said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) and the main contractor China Communications Construction Company Ltd (CCCC) need to work to expedite the process so that the service from Kelantan to Selangor can commence by the end of this year.
“We are trying to see how the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) can help facilitate matters related to the testing and certification processes to expedite this project without compromising safety.
“Usually, it takes two to three months, so we want to see how we can shorten that time,” he said at a press conference after the launch of the Comprehensive Inspection Train (CIT) and the Introduction of the Main ECRL Station Design Concept, as well as the Start of the SIT and FFR ECRL Project at the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station here today.
Loke said the effort to accelerate the operation was made based on the assessment that various tests on the train had been conducted before it was sent to Malaysia, including tests at the factory in China.
According to him, the SIT ECRL starting this month will test the integration of various systems including electrical and signalling systems before the FFR is implemented in September.
He said the first train set and E-Loco each need to undergo FFR over a distance of 8,000 kilometres under the supervision of APAD to ensure that operational safety and reliability meet the established standards and legal requirements.
“FFR is one of the important processes before commercial operations because the train will move on the track under real conditions, but without carrying passengers,” he said.
Loke said that all previous tests must be completed and approved before the FFR is implemented, therefore the effort to expedite the period does not mean that any safety processes will be overlooked.
“We are more afraid than you. I am more afraid than you if there is a risk. Of course, we take all considerations into account,” he said.
Meanwhile, he also said the ECRL project has now recorded an overall progress of 95.08 per cent as of July for Phase 1, which connects Kota Bharu and Gombak.
He added that Phase 2, which connects Gombak to Port Klang, is expected to be completed by December 2027, with operations scheduled to begin in January 2028.
Also present at the event were the Chief Secretary to the Government and MRL chairman Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Haji Habibollah, the Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, and Ministry of Transport secretary-general Datuk Seri M. Jana Santhiran, MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak and CCCC president Zhang Bingnan. — Bernama

Title: Nurul Izzah’s PKR leave has no end date yet, says party sec-gen
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has not set a timeframe for deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar’s leave from party duties as she plans to pursue further studies.
PKR secretary-general Senator Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the party was prepared to welcome Nurul Izzah back to her duties when she was ready to resume her responsibilities.
“The deputy president will go on leave after the party’s National Congress.
“Just for this three-day event, she would continue to fulfil her duties, including officiating the AMK and Wanita congress, debate and winding up sessions, as well as delivering her closing remarks.”
Fuziah said this at a press conference after the opening of the 2026 National Congress of Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) and Wanita PKR, which was officiated by Nurul Izzah, at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh today.
Meanwhile, Fuziah said PKR president’s policy speech was expected to address the party’s struggle, direction and future, as well as its institutional reform agenda.
“It is up to the delegates to decide which motions they want to bring forward and debate, including those on strengthening the party,” she added. — Bernama

Title: Jobless single dad claims trial to robbing and injuring mum with baby at Batu Gajah house
Article:
IPOH, Aug 14 — An unemployed man pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of robbing and causing injury to a woman last week.
Lee Koon Yew, 49, was charged with committing the offence against Fatin Fazira Ahmad Fauzi, 26, at a house in Taman Batu Gajah Perdana at 11.40 am on Aug 8.
The charge, under Section 394 of the Penal Code, carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years, as well as a fine or whipping, upon conviction.
Judge Norhayati Mohamad Yunus set bail at RM8,000 with one surety and ordered the accused to report to the nearest police station once a month, surrender his passport to the court and refrain from interfering with witnesses.
The court fixed Sept 23 for mention of the case.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor M. Raveena proposed bail of RM20,000 with one surety.
“At the time of the incident, the victim was carrying her two-month-old baby, and the injuries sustained required her to undergo hospital treatment,” she said.
Lawyer Dhirren Amaresha, representing Lee, appealed for minimal bail, saying his client was a single father of two and suffered from high blood pressure.
On Aug 8, a 53-second video went viral on social media showing a man attempting to flee on a motorcycle after an alleged robbery.
The following day, Batu Gajah District Police Chief ACP Md Noor Aehawan Mohammad said police had arrested a man suspected of involvement in the robbery and assault at the house in Taman Batu Gajah Perdana. — Bernama

Title: Penang exco says traffic fixes before proposed Tanjung Bungah–Batu Ferringhi reclamation project
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — The identification of the coastal area from Tanjung Bungah to Batu Ferringhi as a potential area for reclamation in the Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (Review) (RSNPP 2040) does not mean that the state government has decided to implement the project.
State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the area was only identified as a location with potential for future reclamation based on studies including geographical and hydrological aspects.
“However, whether it will continue or when it will be implemented, that has not been decided by the state government,” he told reporters at Komtar when commenting on the new reclamation area identified in the final draft of RSNPP 2040 involving the coastline between Tanjung Bungah and Batu Ferringhi.
Zairil said the same thing happened when the Middle Bank area was identified as a potential area for reclamation in the previous structure plan, but it was not implemented.
He stressed that the state government can from time to time identify areas with potential for reclamation as part of long-term planning, but the implementation of a project remains subject to the state government’s consideration and decision.
Meanwhile, Zairil, who is also the Tanjong Bunga State assemblyman said any large-scale reclamation proposal in the northern part of the island, including Batu Ferringhi, must first consider solutions to traffic congestion issues.
The final draft of the RSNPP 2040 is reported to identify new reclamation areas along the northern coast of Penang, including Batu Ferringhi, with the proposal known as the “Penang Gateway” having the potential to stimulate growth in the tourism, services, trade and property development sectors. — Bernama

Title: Three months’ jail for man pleading guilty to offensive X posts against Terengganu royalty
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 14 — A man was sentenced to three months’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to five charges of making offensive posts against the Terengganu royalty via X.
Judge Ahmad Fuad Othman handed down the sentence against Azman Hakim Hassanuddin, 35, and ordered the jail term to run from his remand date of June 24.
He stressed that offences touching on the royal institution, religion and racial sensitivities must be taken seriously because they can have a wide impact on society.
Ahmad Fuad said the principles of Decency and Morality and Loyalty to the King and Country, as enshrined in the Rukun Negara, must be respected.
“So we are sensitive when it comes to the royalty. We respect our rulers. That means we protect them and hold them in high esteem. When you commit such acts, you diminish the dignity of the rulers,” he said.
The judge said 3R-related offences, touching on religion, race, and the royal institution, can trigger a ripple effect, where insults against religion or race can provoke outrage and attacks on the royal institution can undermine its dignity and standing.
Earlier, the prosecution informed the court that based on a report from Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta dated Aug 10, the accused, who is a mental health patient, was found fit to stand trial and capable of defending himself.
On June 24, deputy public prosecutor Fadhli Ab Wahab had applied for the accused to be sent to a psychiatric hospital for observation and evaluation.
In his appeal, the accused requested a fine instead, saying he still requires treatment and daily medication.
He said he was only sleeping two to three hours a day when he made the posts in February due to his severe condition.
Azman Hakim was accused of creating and transmitting offensive and threatening communications via his X account @gmxn_ on Feb 19.
He was charged with making four separate offensive posts between 2.25 pm and 4.29 pm with the intent to annoy others.
On a separate charge, he was accused of making a threatening post at 3.46 pm with the intent to intimidate someone.
The charges were brought under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which carries a fine not exceeding RM500,000, or imprisonment of up to two years, or both, as well as an additional fine of RM5,000 for each day the offence persists after conviction. — Bernama

Title: Sabah looks to grow Kinabalu Unesco geopark with Tuaran’s natural treasures
Article:
TUARAN, Aug 14 — The Sabah government is studying a proposal to expand the Kinabalu Unesco Global Geopark (KUGGp) to include parts of Tuaran district, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said preliminary findings from the Geo-Sulaman Scientific Expedition in April 2025 showed that Tuaran has unique geological features, rich biodiversity, significant cultural heritage and valuable community knowledge.
“These assets should be studied and documented carefully and, where appropriate, incorporated into a broader conservation and sustainable development framework to strengthen Sabah’s ecological connectivity and ecotourism,” he said at the closing ceremony of the KUGGp Revalidation Mission at the Rumpun Bajau Sama Cultural Centre in Lok Batik here today.
His speech was delivered by Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin.
Hajiji said KUGGp currently covers an area of about 4,750 square kilometres across three districts, namely Kota Belud, Kota Marudu and parts of Ranau.
“Managing an area of this size, involving multiple administrative jurisdictions and diverse communities, requires a clear and coordinated long-term strategy.
“In this regard, the Kinabalu Unesco Global Geopark Management Plan 2026-2035 replaces the Interim Management Plan 2021-2025.
“The new plan integrates the geopark’s key pillars, namely resource conservation, research, education and socioeconomic development, and will be implemented in three phases – foundation building, acceleration and transformation – guided by nine strategic themes towards 2035,” he said.
He said the KUGGp Revalidation Mission, which began on Aug 10, was not merely about maintaining Unesco recognition, but was an opportunity to strengthen institutions, improve management, enhance community participation and ensure Unesco’s values were translated into tangible action on the ground.
According to him, Unesco recognition must provide more than international prestige by creating meaningful and sustainable opportunities for communities through responsible tourism and geotourism, community-based enterprises, local product development, cultural experiences, education, skills training, employment opportunities and participation in decision-making processes.
“This approach is in line with the Sabah Maju Jaya 2.0 development plan for 2026-2030, which aims to drive a more competitive, inclusive and sustainable Sabah, while ensuring development contributes to the well-being of our people.
“For KUGGp, this means expanding market access, strengthening local entrepreneurship, improving appropriate infrastructure and ensuring communities become active partners in shaping development, rather than merely passive beneficiaries,” he said.
The Chief Minister expressed his appreciation to Unesco assessors Dr Zhang Yuanhai and Dr Atsuko Niina for their expertise and diligence throughout the 2026 KUGGp Revalidation Mission.
He said every Unesco Global Geopark undergoes revalidation every four years, and the process was important not only to maintain international recognition but also to ensure that the geopark continues to meet the standards, principles and responsibilities set by Unesco.
“We also thank the KUGGp scientific advisers, Sabah Parks as the lead agency, federal and state government agencies, institutions of higher learning, district offices, local authorities, community leaders and local communities, as well as every organisation and individual whose efforts contributed to the success of this revalidation mission,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Not just train stops: ECRL stations are getting a Malaysian glow-up, telling East Coast stories
Article:
GOMBAK, Aug 14 — Every major East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) station is an architectural tribute to its state’s heritage, history, and culture, transforming each stop into a living showcase of local identity, not just a transit point.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said this approach ensures ECRL development highlights the cultural and heritage uniqueness of communities along its route.
“For example, the Kota Bharu ECRL Station in Bandar Batu Tunjong features the traditional ‘Rumah Meleh Melayu’ architectural concept with ‘Bunga Ketam Guri’ motifs, preserving Kelantan’s cultural identity within a modern development.
“The Kuala Terengganu Station design, meanwhile, is inspired by boat and wave elements, symbolising Terengganu’s maritime identity, a fitting tribute to its proud heritage of hand-carved traditional wooden boat-making,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Comprehensive Inspection Train (CIT), unveiling of ECRL’s main station design concepts, and the start of System Integration Testing (SIT) and Fault-Free Run (FFR) at the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station today.
Loke said in Pahang the KotaSAS Station design is inspired by the state crest, featuring the ‘Gading Gajah’ (elephant tusk), while the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station draws inspiration from the Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, a 14-kilometre-long quartz formation.
He said the geometric concept of the Gombak station is derived from the quartz ridge’s natural fort-like shape, symbolising natural beauty.
The 26-month development on the 9.96-hectare site has now reached 98.96 per cent, and is expected to be fully completed this September.
Loke said overall progress for ECRL Phase 1, linking Kota Bharu and Gombak, has reached 95.08 per cent as of July.
“With this encouraging progress, I believe the public will soon experience the ECRL services as scheduled. The East Coast community can look forward to returning home for Hari Raya Aidilfitri on the ECRL next year,” he said.
The ECRL project is now entering its testing and commissioning phase through SIT and FFR for the Kota Bharu-Gombak stretch, paving the way for commercial operations targeted to begin this December, ahead of the original January target.
Meanwhile, China Communications Construction Company Ltd (CCCC) president Zhang Bingnan said the start of SIT and FFR marks a significant step toward the project’s completion, handover and smooth operation.
He said CCCC remains committed to high standards, quality and efficiency in delivering a durable rail system that benefits communities along the route. — Bernama

Title: A way out after 23 years? Govt offers Semantan Estate settlement in Duta Enclave dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — After more than two decades of legal battles over 106 hectares of prime Kuala Lumpur land now occupied by major federal institutions, the government has offered Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd a settlement to resolve its compensation claim.
The offer was disclosed at the High Court here today, where both parties informed Justice Roslan Mat Nor that Putrajaya had extended the settlement proposal, although its terms and value were not disclosed, news outlet
Free Malaysia Today
reported.
“Under the circumstances, we would like to settle the case as soon as possible. But to be fair to (Semantan), I’m sure they will need some time to confer with their client before they can decide as to whether the matter can be settled amicably,” senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan was quoted as saying in court.
Semantan Estate applied to postpone today’s hearing to give the company time to consider the offer, but Roslan rejected the application and ordered the hearing to proceed as scheduled.
Nurhafizza said the government had only received instructions to extend the settlement offer yesterday, as all settlement proposals must first be approved by the Finance Ministry.
The dispute dates back to 2003, when Semantan Estate sued the government over its 106ha parcel in Kuala Lumpur known as the Duta Enclave, claiming that the land had been unlawfully acquired in 1956.
The disputed land along Jalan Tuanku Abdul Halim, formerly Jalan Duta, now houses several federal facilities, including the National Hockey Stadium, National Archives, Kuala Lumpur Syariah Court, Inland Revenue Board and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Academy.
The High Court ruled in Semantan Estate’s favour in 2009, but subsequent appellate decisions found that the company was not entitled to the land title.
The case took a significant turn on June 24 last year when the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was entitled to adequate compensation instead, with the amount to be assessed based on the land’s value in 1956 when the government took possession of it.
The appellate court also ordered an assessment of mesne profits, meaning compensation for the government’s use or occupation of the disputed land during the relevant period.
The Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal on November 13 last year, leaving the Court of Appeal’s ruling in force and paving the way for the compensation assessment now before the High Court.
The settlement offer now gives both sides a possible route to resolve the financial dispute without waiting for the assessment process to run its full course.
Semantan Estate has yet to accept the offer and the terms remain undisclosed, according to the news portal.
The hearing continued today with chartered surveyor Foo Gee Jen called to testify.
The separate assessment of mesne profits is being heard before High Court judge Ahmad Shahrir Salleh.
The hearing before Roslan continues on August  21.
Semantan Estate is represented by lawyers Janet Chai, Ira Biswas and Alexie Ng.

Title: KLIA Transit offers 50pc return fare discount to Putrajaya, Cyberjaya for National Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Express Rail Link Sdn Bhd (ERL) is offering a 50 per cent discount on KLIA Transit return tickets to Putrajaya and Cyberjaya in conjunction with Malaysia’s 69th National Day celebrations.
In a press statement today, ERL said the promotion covers journeys from KL Sentral, Bandar Tasik Selatan and Salak Tinggi between August 29 and 31.
Discounted tickets for adults and children aged six to 15 will be available exclusively through the KLIA Ekspres mobile app and official website from August 26 to 31.
The promotion does not apply to travel to KLIA Terminal 1 or Terminal 2.
Children aged five and below can travel free with every adult ticket purchased, subject to a maximum of three children per adult.
ERL will also give an exclusive Merdeka Pack to the first 200 passengers arriving at Putrajaya and Cyberjaya Station on August 31.
Free shuttle buses provided by Prasarana and Perbadanan Putrajaya will take passengers from Putrajaya Sentral to event locations around the administrative capital, including the National Day parade and its full-dress rehearsal.

Title: Sim Tze Tzin dismisses PKR turmoil talk, says core leadership united under Anwar
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — PKR strategy director Sim Tze Tzin today dismissed claims of internal turmoil in the party, saying its core leadership remains united under president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Sim said the party’s upcoming national convention would provide delegates with a platform to raise concerns following electoral setbacks in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, while allowing leaders to identify and address weaknesses before the next general election.
“Of course, delegates will raise various issues and this is a platform for the leadership to hear their grievances and find solutions,” he told reporters at a press conference in Komtar here.
“We need to understand our weaknesses and work hard over the next year before the general election. There is still time for us to improve,” he added.
He said PKR’s Angkatan Muda Keadilan and Wanita wings had begun their conventions last night, while the party’s national convention would take place tomorrow.
Sim said PKR was not involved in any vote this weekend, referring to the separate DAP convention.
On a statement by PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar warning that the party would be weakened by having “two captains” and internal disputes, Sim said he had yet to read the full remarks and was therefore not in a position to comment.
However, he said he saw no internal upheaval in PKR.
“The leadership is very solid. The core leaders remain steadfast in the party,” he said.
Sim acknowledged that several MPs, including the Subang MP, had left PKR, but said their departures had long been anticipated.
“We have known for some time about the movements of a small group of leaders who had planned to do so, and the party has moved on,” he said.
“The core team remains intact and is working very well within the party leadership,” he said.
When asked whether PKR had two leaders at its helm, Sim said the party had only one “captain”.
“How can PKR have two captains? Our only captain is the prime minister, who is also the party president.
“I think this is very clear in Keadilan. There is only one general — unlike Perikatan Nasional, which has many issues and various captains. In Keadilan, we have only one, namely Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim,” he said.

Title: Chow Kon Yeow says Penang DAP takes no stance, leaves Cabinet exit motion to delegates
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Penang DAP has not adopted an official position on a motion calling for the party to leave the Cabinet, instead leaving the decision to its delegates at the DAP Convention on Sunday.
DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow said Penang delegates had been briefed on the motions to be debated and voted on at the convention.
“Each state has its own way of approaching the convention that will take place this Sunday.
“For Penang, the state committee met last Wednesday and we took an open approach,” he said.
He said Penang DAP did not take an official state position.
“We are allowing the delegates to make the decision,” he told a press conference at the Chief Minister’s Office in Komtar here today.
The DAP Convention on Sunday is expected to provide a platform for delegates to debate and decide on several matters, including a motion on DAP’s position in the unity government.
Chow, who is also Penang Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the motion specifically concerned a proposal for DAP to leave the Cabinet while continuing to support the unity government.
“The motion concerns whether DAP will leave the Cabinet but continue to support the unity government. That is the motion,” he said.

Title: ‘Being popular alone is not enough’: Youth chief tells PKR leaders to rebuild grassroots strength
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 14 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) needs to put forward a more compelling narrative to strengthen people’s confidence in the party, said Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim.
He said grassroots strength must also be further strengthened and translated into victories in the next election.
“Being popular alone is not enough. Having gone through the Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections, there is one thing, and I believe everyone agrees, that our grassroots strength is not yet strong enough to translate into victories.
“Since 1998, we have entered elections riding waves of support, with the people at the time becoming part of our machinery, and until today when we have formed the government,” he said in his speech at the 2026 AMK National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre in Ayer Keroh today.
The congress, which was opened by PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, was also attended by PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa and Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek.
Muhammad Kamil said the situation required the party to renew its approach, strategy and political activities so that its journey would be more organised, structured and targeted, given that pursuing reform while in and out of government presented different challenges.
Therefore, he urged the party’s members and leadership not to lose heart, but instead to accept the bitter reality that the people had sent a clear signal, calling on the party to rise again for their sake.
Meanwhile, Fadhlina, in her speech, said the congress should serve as a platform for self-reflection, acknowledging weaknesses, listening to the grassroots and formulating an action agenda to strengthen the party.
She said the leaders’ speeches should be embraced and refined into an action agenda, strengthening the organisation, enhancing the fighting spirit, forging new strength and ultimately winning the next election.
“Brothers and sisters, take this opportunity to truly digest all the speeches by the leaders. Use this platform for self-reflection, to acknowledge our weaknesses and shortcomings with full awareness and humility.
“The delegates’ debates should serve as recommendations from the grassroots to further strengthen the party,” she said. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia: Sarawak’s hot, dry spell could keep haze hanging around till Aug 20 while thunderstorms lash peninsula
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Hot and relatively dry weather is expected to persist in Sarawak and several other areas of Borneo until Aug 20, potentially increasing the risk of haze and reducing visibility, particularly in southern Sarawak.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement today, said the conditions were influenced by southerly winds and the still-high number of hotspots in Borneo.
As of 10am today, 10 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index readings at unhealthy levels, based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, with the majority of the locations in Sarawak.
Meanwhile, in a separate statement, MetMalaysia issued a thunderstorm and heavy rain warning for the whole of Perlis, Kedah, Penang and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 1pm today.
The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung and Bagan Datuk, as well as Selangor, including Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling, Gombak and Hulu Selangor.
The public is advised to stay updated on the latest weather information and warnings through MetMalaysia’s website, official social media platforms and the myCuaca app. — Bernama

Title: Pulau Jerejak as financial hub? Putrajaya backs plan to boost Penang’s high-tech sector
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Pulau Jerejak has the potential to be developed as a financial hub to complement the semiconductor and high-tech sector in Bayan Lepas.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said based on a briefing from developer Ideal Property, about 32.37 hectares on Pulau Jerejak are slated for an integrated development.
The project comprises a financial centre, resort, serviced apartments and hotel, creating an ecosystem that can attract investors to set up operations there.
“Penang is the high-tech industry hub of Malaysia, but we lack money and investors. We even lack financial institutions to help take our tech companies to the next level.
“We need investors, so I think this Pulau Jerejak project will be good to complement our high-tech sector,” he told reporters after distributing Jalur Gemilang flags in conjunction with Merdeka Day at a food premises in Sungai Nibong today.
Sim, who is also Bayan Baru MP, said the government supports turning the area into a financial zone to attract venture capitalists, banks and private equity firms to open offices near the Bayan Lepas industrial area.
Sim explained that about 85 per cent of Pulau Jerejak has been gazetted as a forest reserve. Development is only allowed on land acquired by the developer and is subject to height restrictions because the area lies within flight paths.
On a related note, he said a new bridge connecting Pulau Jerejak to the Penang mainland is expected to support the island’s development.
He said the one-kilometre bridge is estimated to cost RM500 million, with preliminary road-widening works scheduled to begin next month.
“It is expected to take three years to complete, with a target date of March 2029. It will have four lanes, as well as pedestrian and bicycle paths,” he said.
He said access to the bridge is planned from the roundabout near Queensbay and Jambatan Harapan, linking to the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway.
Sim has proposed an iconic bridge design to turn it into a landmark, and the developer has agreed to bring in two international designers and a local architect to bring the vision to life.
The Penang Island City Council approved planning permission for the redevelopment of Jerejak Rainforest Resort and mixed-use development in March 2018, while the state government gave the green light for the bridge connecting Pulau Jerejak to the mainland. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia could become high-income nation by 2029 as tech drives exports, says deputy minister
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Malaysia has the potential to achieve high-income nation status in the next two to three years if the people continue to work hard and remain united in driving the country’s progress.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Malaysia is currently classified as an upper middle-income country, and recent economic developments, including the country’s trade performance, indicate that it is moving in a positive direction.
He said such confidence was underpinned by the nation’s trade performance in the first half of 2026, where it rose by 22.4 per cent to RM1.79 trillion.
“Exports expanded by 27.5 per cent to RM971.6 billion while imports stood at RM824.44 billion, leading to a trade surplus of RM147.15 billion,” he said to reporters during the Jalur Gemilang flag distribution ceremony in conjunction with the upcoming Merdeka Day here today.
Sim, who is also the Bayan Baru member of Parliament, said trade in June had reached RM340.88 billion – the highest monthly tally recorded in the nation’s history – and added that more than half of the country’s exports in the first six months of this year comprised technology-based products.
He said the country’s export structure has also undergone a significant transformation, with electrical and electronic (E&E) products – including semiconductors – accounting for 42.5 per cent of exports, while machinery and equipment contributed 12.6 per cent.
“We’re slowly moving towards becoming a technological country, with E&E, machines, and high-tech products accounting for more than half of our total exports. So this is a success story for Malaysia,” he said.
Sim said this achievement should motivate Malaysians to continue nurturing the spirit of patriotism and strengthening unity in accelerating the country’s development.
He added that in the nearly seven decades of independence, the country has undergone a major transformation, from an economy that once depended heavily on traditional sectors to one with growing technological capabilities. — Bernama

Title: Teo Nie Ching insists Johor DAP won’t dictate, delegates hold Cabinet fate in Sunday congress
Article:
KULAI, Aug 14 — Johor DAP delegates are free to decide whether the party’s leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of the special congress this Sunday.
Johor DAP chief Teo Nie Ching said the state leadership is leaving it to more than 400 delegates, who have the freedom to make decisions based on their respective views and understanding of the party’s direction.
“In Johor, the state party does not have a single position or stance on the matter. We give the freedom to the delegates or representatives to make that decision at DAP’s national congress this Sunday.
“Johor DAP even held a dialogue session yesterday with party’s secretary-general Anthony Loke to explain the issue.
“Regardless of the session, the party’s state leadership chose to give delegates the freedom to make their own decisions,” she told reporters after attending an allocation handover event at Sekolah Kebangsaan Murni Jaya here today.
Teo, who is also the DAP’s national vice chairman, was responding to media queries on the party’s Johor state decision ahead of the national congress that is expected to determine whether the party should remain in the government.
It was previously reported that a motion on the decision would be tabled by more than 4,000 delegates at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) in Putrajaya.
Teo, who is also the Kulai MP, said that Johor DAP would accept and abide by any decision made at the congress.
She said Johor is one of the states with a fairly high representation among delegates attending.
“I believe there are members who can represent their respective branches and understand the situation based on the party’s struggle and principles.
“I am of the opinion that they will make the right call based on the party’s direction and the country,” she said.
DAP’s congress this Sunday at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) is expected to focus on the party’s position in the federal unity government.
The congress comes amid growing debate over slow reforms and electoral setbacks within the party, including whether it should remain part of the administration under Anwar.

Title: Malaysia’s inflation outlook steady at 1.5–2.5 pc, BNM stresses external pressures remain manageable
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia’s headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 1.6 per cent in the preceding quarter, while core inflation moderated to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said today.
BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said higher input costs had so far seen limited pass through to consumer prices.
He noted that almost 80 per cent of firms are facing higher cost pressures, but only about half indicated they may pass these costs on to consumers, as demand remains weak.
The central bank’s figures showed producer cost pressures were concentrated at the upstream stage, with crude materials prices rising 27.5 per cent and intermediate inputs 3.7 per cent, while finished goods prices increased 1.4 per cent.
Headline inflation is projected to average 1.5 to 2.5 per cent in 2026, with BNM saying the overall impact of external cost pressures is expected to remain contained.
Expanding further, Abdul Rasheed said the increase in headline inflation mainly reflected higher external cost pressures following the conflict in the Middle East.
Fuel prices, particularly RON97 and diesel, increased during the quarter, leading to fuel inflation of 5 per cent, compared with minus 1.5 per cent in the first quarter.
He added that producer cost pressures remained concentrated at the upstream stage, with limited pass-through to later stages of production and broader consumer prices during the quarter.
“Core inflation moderated mainly due to softer inflation in jewellery and watches, which eased to 23.7 per cent from 39.1 per cent, and rent, which moderated to 1.4 per cent from 1.6 per cent.
“Inflation pervasiveness, measured by the share of Consumer Price Index items registering monthly price increases, rose to 45.5 per cent from 38.3 per cent in the first quarter, close to its historical average of 45.6 per cent,” he said.
According to Abdul Rasheed, the increase was driven mainly by a sharp rise in April before moderating in May and June.
He also said high-frequency indicators showed food prices had rebounded from earlier declines, returning close to pre-conflict levels.
Additionally, Abdul Rasheed said the impact of the Middle East conflict on inflation remained an area that required close monitoring.
“The Middle East conflict is still very nascent, and we need to be listening in terms of what could be the impact on the commodity prices, what could be the impact to prices, and how this would then affect prices in Malaysia,” he said.
As of early August, inflation outcomes and high-frequency indicators remained broadly in line with the projections, he said.
However, the outlook remains subject to upside risks, mainly from external uncertainties.
He reminded that further escalation of the Middle East conflict could push global commodity prices higher, while larger and more persistent input cost pressures could arise from broader supply chain disruptions, including adverse weather conditions.
At the same time, softer global demand could weigh on commodity prices and inflation, while further improvements in global supply conditions could ease cost pressures.
“Overall, inflation is projected to remain moderate, while the external cost pressures may place some upward pressure on prices,” Abdul Rasheed said.
He said stable domestic demand conditions, together with targeted government measures such as fuel subsidies, were expected to continue limiting the pass-through to consumer prices.
Meanwhile, Abdul Rasheed said the Monetary Policy Committee maintained the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent at its July 2026 meeting, saying the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate and consistent with the outlook for continued price stability and sustainable economic growth.
Asked whether the political cycle could make BNM reluctant to raise the OPR even if economic data and key indicators pointed to a need to do so, Abdul Rasheed said the MPC would remain guided by data and its price stability objective.
He said BNM would continue to monitor developments that could affect the inflation outlook, including whether price increases were becoming sticky and persistent.

Title: One year after son attacked, Rafizi decries threats, says case ‘died off’ unresolved
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — After a year since the attack on his child in Putrajaya, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has claimed the case has “gone quiet and died off”.
“A year has passed, and the case has gone quiet,” he wrote on Facebook, adding that he had been informally told by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail of a suspected mastermind, but his request for an open statement in Parliament was rejected.
He stressed that such an attack was unprecedented in Malaysia. “Never before has a child been assaulted and a wife threatened simply because of her husband’s political stance,” he said.
Rafizi claimed the assault was intended to pressure his wife into forcing him to retire from politics. He thanked his family for standing firm, saying: “If I bowed to such threats, I would be complicit in allowing wrongdoing, damage and crime to continue in this country.”
He warned that if such methods could be used against the child of a former minister, ordinary citizens could face similar intimidation.
Rafizi vowed to continue seeking justice. “I will wait for 13 August every year until the attacker and those behind them are brought to justice. Even if the authorities do not act, I know they will have to answer in the hereafter,” he said.
Recalling the incident on August 13 last year, Rafizi said his child was attacked in public while attempting to enter a car. He recounted that the assailant, dressed in dark rider’s clothing and wearing a helmet, grabbed his child by the neck and injected him twice in the shoulder while shouting at his wife. He added that his wife later received WhatsApp messages threatening that “the next would be HIV.”
In January, Saifuddin Nasution stated that certain information could not be disclosed to avoid jeopardising investigations or witness safety, adding that the case remained under probe pending new leads.
